en: A process of decision-making that seeks widespread agreement among group members.
General agreement among the members of a given group or community, each member of which exercises some discretion in decision-making and …
To seek consensus; to hold discussions with the aim of reaching mutual agreement.

consensus.ety: Borrowed from Latin cōnsēnsus (“agreement, accordance, unanimity”), from cōnsentiō (“feel together; agree”); see consent.

ex.en: At present, consensus has yet to be reached.
ex.ja: 今のところ、全体の意見の一致には至っていない。

ex.en: Can we reach a consensus on this issue?
ex.ja: 私たちはこの問題に関して合意に達することが出来るだろうか。

ex.en: The people did not reach consensus on taxation.
ex.ja: 国民は税制に関しては意見が一致しなかった。

note.ja: con（共に）+ sens（感じる）+ us。皆が同じように感じること →「合意・総意」。

en: An emphatic or formal act of saying, telling or asserting something, by speech or writing; a decisive assertion or proclamation.
A list of items for various legal purposes, e.g. customs declaration.

declaration.ety: From Middle English declaration, declaracion, declaracioun, from Old French declaration (French déclaration), from Latin dēclārātiōnem, accusative of Latin dēclārātiō.

ex.en: Please fill out the Customs Declaration Form.
ex.ja: 税関申告書に記入してください。

ex.en: A customs declaration is required.
ex.ja: 関税申告書が必要になります。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ clar（明らかな）+ ation。はっきり明らかにすること →「宣言・申告」。

en: Any of several annual horse races.
Any organized race.

derby.ety: From Epsom Derby horse race, named after Edward Smith-Stanley, 12th Earl of Derby. Ultimately from Derby.

ex.en: Don't you think my horse ought to win the Derby?
ex.ja: 私の馬がダービーに勝つとは思いませんか。

ex.en: His horse ran in the Derby.
ex.ja: 彼の馬はダービーに出走した。

ex.en: Derby Day is Wednesday fortnight.
ex.ja: ダービー競馬の日は２週間後の水曜日だ。

note.ja: イングランドのダービー伯爵（Earl of Derby）が創設した競馬から。地名ダービー（Derby）が由来。

en: That which distinguishes; a single occurrence of a determining factor or feature, the fact of being divided; separation, discrimination.
The act of distinguishing, discriminating; discrimination.

distinction.ety: From Middle English distinccioun, from Old French distinction (attested from the 12th century), borrowed from Latin distinctiōnem, action noun of distinguō (“separate, distinguish”). By surface analysis, distinct (“to distinguish”) + -ion. Attested in English from the late 14th century.

ex.en: I can make a distinction between good and bad.
ex.ja: 私にだって善悪に区別はつく。

ex.en: The distinction in usage between the two words is clear.
ex.ja: その２語の用法の区別は明瞭である。

ex.en: He advocated abolishing class distinctions.
ex.ja: 彼は階級差別の廃止を主張した。

note.ja: dis（離して）+ stinct（刺す・印をつける）+ ion。印をつけて区別すること →「区別・違い・卓越」。distinguish（区別する）、instinct（中を刺すもの→本能）も同じ。

en: A voluntary gift or contribution for a specific cause.
The act of giving or bestowing; a grant.

donation.ety: From Middle English donacion, donation, from Middle French donation, from Latin dōnātiō (“a present”), from dōnō (“to give”), from dōnum (“a gift”). Recorded in English since the 15th century. Equivalent to donate + -ion.

ex.en: Donations are important for development to continue.
ex.ja: 開発の継続に寄付は大切です。

ex.en: Corporate political donations are coming under heavy scrutiny.
ex.ja: 企業の政治献金は厳しい検査の対象になっています。

ex.en: Thank you very much for your generous donation.
ex.ja: 多額の寄付をありがとうございました。

note.ja: don（与える）+ ation。与えること →「寄付・寄贈」。donor（提供者）も同じ。

en: Of or affecting the face.
Concerned with or used in improving the appearance of the face.
A personal care beauty treatment which involves cleansing and moisturizing of the human face.
A kind of early silent film focusing on the facial expressions of the actor.

facial.ety:

ex.en: Observe his facial reaction when we mention a price.
ex.ja: 価格について触れたときに彼の顔に出る反応を観察しなさい。

ex.en: I want to pluck your facial hair.
ex.ja: あなたの髭を抜きたいです。

ex.en: The dog has various facial expressions.
ex.ja: 犬にはいろいろな表情があります。

note.ja: face（顔）+ -ial。「顔の」→ 顔の手入れ「フェイシャル」。

en: Loyal; adhering firmly to person or cause.
Having faith.
The practicing members of a religion or followers of a cause.
Someone or something that is faithful or reliable.

faithful.ety: From Middle English feithful, equivalent to faith + -ful.

ex.en: You must, above all, be faithful to your friends.
ex.ja: 何よりもまず友人に誠実でなければならない。

ex.en: Because dogs are more faithful than cats.
ex.ja: なぜなら犬の方が猫より忠実ですから。

ex.en: You must be faithful to your word.
ex.ja: 約束には忠実でなくてはいけない。

note.ja: faith（信頼）+ ful。ラテン語 fides（信頼）から →「忠実な・誠実な・正確な」。

en: Causing death or destruction.
Causing a sudden end to the running of a program.
A fatality; an event that leads to death.
A fatal error; a failure that causes a program to terminate.

fatal.ety: From Middle French fatal, from Latin fātālis (“fatal”).

ex.en: The scandal was fatal to his political future.
ex.ja: そのスキャンダルは彼の政治的将来に致命的であった。

ex.en: Today is the fatal day that they will attempt their escape.
ex.ja: きょうこそは彼らが脱走を企てる運命の日だ。

ex.en: Lack of oxygen is fatal to most animals.
ex.ja: 酸素が不足することは大部分の動物にとって命にかかわることである。

note.ja: ラテン語 fatum（運命・神の言葉）から。運命を決する →「致命的な・決定的な」。fate（運命）。

en: The fruit of the fig tree, pear-shaped and containing many small seeds.
A fruit-bearing tree or shrub of the genus Ficus that is native mainly to the tropics.
To move suddenly or quickly; rove about.

fig.ety: From Middle English fige, fygge (also fyke, from Old English fīc, see fike), borrowed from Anglo-Norman figue, borrowed from Old French figue, from Old Occitan figa, from Vulgar Latin *fīca (“fig”), from Latin fīcus (“fig tree”), from a pre-Indo European language, perhaps Phoenician 𐤐𐤂 (pg, literally “ripe fig”) (compare Biblical Hebrew פַּגָּה (paggâ, “early fallen fig”), Classical Syriac ܦܓܐ (paggāʾ), dialectal Arabic فَجّ (fajj), فِجّ (fijj)). (Another Semitic root (compare Akkadian 𒈠 (tīʾu, literally “fig”)) was borrowed into Ancient Greek as σῦκον (sûkon) (whence English sycophant; Boeoti

ex.en: The figs on the market are too expensive.
ex.ja: 市場で売ってるイチジクは高すぎるよ。

ex.en: He doesn't give a fig about money.
ex.ja: 彼は金のことはちっとも気にしていない。

ex.en: I love those big, green figs.
ex.ja: 私はそれらの大きな青いイチジクが大好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 ficus から古フランス語を経た語。「イチジク」。

ex.en: Tom looked genuinely interested.
ex.ja: トムは本当に興味がありそうだった。

note.ja: genuine（本物の）+ -ly。「心から・本当に」。

en: A need or compelling desire for food.
Any strong desire or need.
To be in need of food.
To have a desire (for); to long; to yearn.

hunger.ety:
From Middle English hunger, from Old English hungor (“hunger, desire; famine”), from Proto-West Germanic *hungr, from Proto-Germanic *hungruz, *hunhruz (“hunger”), from Proto-Indo-European *kenk- (“to burn, smart, desire, hunger, thirst”).
Cognate with West Frisian honger, hûnger (“hunger”), Dutch honger (“hunger”), German Low German Hunger (“hunger”), German Hunger (“hunger”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish hunger (“hunger”), Faroese and Icelandic hungur (“hunger”).

ex.en: Some people in the world suffer from hunger.
ex.ja: 世界には飢えに苦しむ人々も居る。

ex.en: She hungered for a sight of her mother.
ex.ja: 彼女は母を一目見たくてたまらなかった。

ex.en: The boy has a hunger for adventure.
ex.ja: その少年は冒険に飢えている。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「空腹・飢え」。→「空腹・飢餓・渇望」。hungry（空腹の）。

en: A severe tropical cyclone; an intense storm rotating around a central eye.
A severe tropical cyclone in the North Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, or in the eastern North Pacific off the west coast …
To be violent, with winds of 119 km/h (74 miles per hour) or greater, usually accompanied by rain, lightning, and thunder.
To move noisily, quickly, and dramatically, becoming the center of attention.

hurricane.ety:
Etymology tree
Taíno *hurakābor.
Spanish huracánbor.
English hurricane
Borrowed from Spanish huracán, ultimately from Taíno *hurakā.

ex.en: The category of a hurricane depends on its wind speed.
ex.ja: ハリケーンの種類は風速によって決まります。

ex.en: Due to the recent hurricane, a lot of people lost their homes.
ex.ja: 最近のハリケーンのために多くの人が家を失った。

ex.en: The death toll from the hurricane climbed to 200.
ex.ja: ハリケーンによる死者の数は２００人にのぼった。

note.ja: カリブの言葉 hurakán（嵐の神）からスペイン語を経て →「ハリケーン」。

en: The act of implicating.
The state of being implicated.

From Middle French implication, from Latin implicationem (accusative of implicatio). Equivalent to implicate + -ion.

ex.en: Her implication in the crime was obvious.
ex.ja: 彼女がその犯罪に関係しているのは明らかだった。

ex.en: What was the implication of his remark?
ex.ja: 彼の発言は含みとして何を言いたかったのですか。

ex.en: The implications of this did not at first sink in.
ex.ja: この事が暗に意味することは最初は理解されなかった。

note.ja: im（中に）+ plic（折る）+ ation。中に折り込まれていること →「含意・影響・関与」。imply（ほのめかす）。

en: Something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade.
The practice of importing.
To bring (something) in from a foreign country, especially for sale or trade.
To load a file into a software application from another version or system.

import.ety: From Middle English importen, from Old French emporter, importer, from Latin importō (“bring in from abroad, import”, verb), from in (“in, at, on; into”) + portō (“to carry, bear; convey”).

ex.en: These goods were imported from abroad in secret.
ex.ja: これらの商品は密かに海外から輸入された。

ex.en: Almost all my records were imported from Germany.
ex.ja: 大半の私のレコードはドイツから輸入されたものだった。

ex.en: Imported cars account for less than eight percent.
ex.ja: 輸入車は８％未満しか占めていない。

note.ja: im（中へ）+ port（運ぶ）。中へ運ぶ →「輸入（する）」、意味を運び込む →「重要性」。

en: Characterized by the creation of new ideas or inventions.
Forward-looking; ahead of current thinking.

ex.en: This building is extremely innovative.
ex.ja: この建物、すごく斬新的ね。

en: The power, right, or authority to interpret and apply the law.
The power or right to exercise authority.

ex.en: This case is outside my jurisdiction.
ex.ja: この件は私の管轄外だ。

note.ja: juris（法の）+ dict（言う）+ ion。法を言い渡す権限 →「司法権・管轄（区域）」。

en: The sound of laughing, produced by air so expelled; any similar sound.
A movement (usually involuntary) of the muscles of the laughing face, particularly of the lips, and of the whole body, with a peculiar ex…

laughter.ety: From Middle English laughter, laghter, laȝter, from Old English hleahtor (“laughter, jubilation, derision”), from Proto-Germanic *hlahtraz (“laughter”), from Proto-Indo-European *klek-, *kleg- (“to shout”). Cognate with German Gelächter (“laughter, hilarity, merriment”), Danish and Norwegian latter (“laughter”), Icelandic hlátur (“laughter”). More at laugh.

ex.en: Humans are the only animals capable of laughter.
ex.ja: 笑うことができる動物は人間だけです。

ex.en: Is laughter a quality of man only?
ex.ja: 笑いは人間だけの特質なのか。

ex.en: They held their sides with laughter at his joke.
ex.ja: 彼の冗談を聞いて彼は腹を抱えて笑っていた。

note.ja: laugh（笑う）+ ter。→「笑い・笑い声」。

en: A yellowish citrus fruit.
A semitropical evergreen tree, Citrus limon, that bears such fruits.
Containing or having the flavour/flavor and/or scent of lemons.
Of the pale yellow colour/color of lemons.
To flavour with lemon.

lemon.ety:
Inherited from Middle English lymon, from Old French lymon (“citrus”), from Arabic لَيْمُون (laymūn) or Classical Persian لِیمُون (līmūn), a variant of Classical Persian لِیمُو (līmū, līmō), from Sanskrit निम्बू (nimbū, “lime”), ultimately from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *limaw or Munda. Doublet of lime.
The fandom sense is named after the erotic anime series Cream Lemon.

ex.en: Do you like tea with milk or lemon?
ex.ja: レモンティーとミルクティーどっちが好き？

ex.en: The car that Tom bought was a lemon.
ex.ja: トムが買った車はひどいものだった。

ex.en: Do you prefer tea with lemon or milk?
ex.ja: レモンティーとミルクティーどっちが好き？

note.ja: アラビア語 laimūn（柑橘）から。→「レモン・（俗）欠陥品」。

en: A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood.
Capacity for exercise or exertion; breath.

lung.ety: From Middle English lunge, longe, from Old English lungen, from Proto-Germanic *lunganjō, an enlargement of *lungô (“the light organ, lung”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁lengʷʰ-, whence ultimately also light. Cognate with West Frisian long, Dutch long, German Lunge, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk lunge, Swedish lunga, Icelandic lunga, and also Russian лёгкое (ljóxkoje) (lung), Ancient Greek ἐλαφρός (elaphrós, “light in weight”) and perhaps Albanian lungë (“blister, bulge”). Compare Latin levis and Old English lēoht (Modern English light). See also lights (“lungs”). Superseded

ex.en: Is there a link between smoking and lung cancer?
ex.ja: 喫煙と肺ガンには関連があるのでしょうか？

ex.en: Smoking is responsible for many cases of lung cancer.
ex.ja: 喫煙が肺がんの原因になっている場合が多い。

ex.en: That man died of lung cancer a week ago.
ex.ja: あの男は一週間前に肺ガンで死んだ。

note.ja: light（軽い）と同じ祖先。軽い臓器（肺は水に浮く）→「肺」。

en: Very strong; possessing might.
Very heavy and powerful.
Very; to a high degree.

mighty.ety:
From Middle English mighty, mightie, mighti, myghty, miȝty, maȝty, from Old English mihtiġ, mehtiġ, meahtiġ, mæhtiġ (“mighty”), from Proto-West Germanic *mahtīg (“mighty”), from Proto-Germanic *mahtīgaz (“mighty”), equivalent to might + -y.
Cognate with Scots michty, mychty, Saterland Frisian machtich, Dutch machtig, German Low German machtig, German mächtig, Swedish mäktig.

ex.en: Spain was one of the world's mightiest nations.
ex.ja: スペインは世界最強の国の一つだった。

ex.en: The pen is mightier than the sword.
ex.ja: 文は武に勝る。

ex.en: I don't like people who act all high and mighty.
ex.ja: 威張る人って、好きじゃないのよね。

note.ja: might（力）+ y。ラテン語 magnus と同じ祖先 *megʰ-。→「強力な・巨大な」。

en: Of, pertaining to, or consisting of money.

monetary.ety: From Middle French monétaire, from Late Latin monētārius (“pertaining to money”), from Latin monētārius (“of a mint”), from monēta (“mint, coinage”), from the presence—from 273 BC to AD 84—of the chief Roman mint at the Templum Iunonis Monetae (“Temple of Juno Moneta”), q.v. Doublet of minter.

ex.en: Interest rates will rise due to monetary tightening.
ex.ja: 金融引き締めで金利が上昇するだろう。

ex.en: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund.
ex.ja: ＩＭＦというのは国際通貨基金を表している。

ex.en: The manufacturing sector is a frenzy over the new monetary policy.
ex.ja: 製造部門は新しい金融政策に動揺しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 moneta（貨幣）から。money と同じ。→「貨幣の・金融の」。

en: The organic process by which an organism assimilates food and uses it for growth and maintenance.
The academic discipline around the scientific study of this process.

nutrition.ety: Borrowed from Middle French nutrition, from Old French nutricion, from Latin nutritio.

ex.en: Good nutrition is vital for an infant's growth.
ex.ja: 十分な栄養摂取は幼児の発育にとって極めて重要です。

ex.en: She is careful about her child's nutrition.
ex.ja: 彼女は子供の栄養に気をつけている。

ex.en: The vitamin pill contains abundant nutrition.
ex.ja: このビタミン剤は栄養分を豊富に含んでいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 nutrire（養う）から。nurse（看護師＝養う人）と同じ。→「栄養（摂取）」。

en: Rock or other material that contains valuable or utilitarian materials; primarily a rock containing metals or gems for which it is typica…

ore.ety:
From Middle English or, oor, blend of Old English ōra (“ore, unwrought metal”), of uncertain origin, and ār (“brass, copper, bronze”), from Proto-West Germanic *aiʀ, from Proto-Germanic *aiz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éyos.
Compare Old Norse eir (“brass, copper”), German ehern (“of metal, of iron”), Gothic 𐌰𐌹𐌶 (aiz, “ore”); also Dutch oer (“ferrous hardpan; bog iron ore”). Compare Latin aes (“bronze, copper”), Avestan 𐬀𐬌𐬌𐬀𐬵 (aiiah), Sanskrit अयस् (áyas, “copper, iron”).

ex.en: Treat the men well and the ore will come.
ex.ja: 人間を大切にすれば石が出る。

ex.en: Iron ore occurs there in abundance.
ex.ja: そこは鉄鉱に富む。

note.ja: 古英語 ār（真鍮）から。→「鉱石」。

en: Any coniferous tree of the genus Pinus.
Any tree (usually coniferous) which resembles a member of this genus in some respect.
To languish; to lose flesh or wear away through distress.
To long, to yearn so much that it causes suffering.

pine.ety: From Middle English pyne, from Old English *pīne, from Proto-West Germanic *pīnā, from Latin pīnus, see there for more. Doublet of pinus. Possibly related to fat.

ex.en: A pine stands in front of his house.
ex.ja: 彼の家の前には松の木が立っている。

ex.en: This is a well-shaped pine tree.
ex.ja: これは格好のよい松の木だ。

ex.en: Tall pine trees form a ring around the lake.
ex.ja: 高い松の木が湖の周囲を取り囲んでいる。

note.ja: 「マツ」はラテン語 pinus から。「思い焦がれる」は古英語 pīnian（苦しめる）からで別語（pain と同系）。

en: In a poor manner or condition; without plenty, or sufficiency, or suitable provision for comfort.
With little or no success; indifferently; with little profit or advantage.
Ill, unwell, sick.

poorly.ety: From Middle English poorly, pouerly, poreliche, poureliche, pouerliche, equivalent to poor + -ly.

ex.en: Thanks to a cold summer, beer has sold poorly.
ex.ja: 冷夏のおかげで、ビールの売れ行きはよくなかった。

ex.en: He is not better off because he is poorly paid.
ex.ja: 給料が低いので彼は暮らし向きがよくならない。

ex.en: Don't despise a man because he is poorly dressed.
ex.ja: 貧しい身なりをしているからといって人を軽蔑するな。

note.ja: poor（下手な）+ -ly。「下手に・不十分に」→（英口語）体調が悪い。

en: To place in an attitude or fixed position, for the sake of effect.
To ask; to set (a test, quiz, riddle, etc.).
Position, posture, arrangement (especially of the human body).
Affectation.

pose.ety: From Middle English pose, from Old English ġeposu pl (“cold in the head; catarrh”, literally “(the) sneezes; (the) snorts”), from Old English pos, ġepos (“sneeze, snort”), from Proto-West Germanic *pos, from Proto-Germanic *pusą (“sneeze, snort”), from Proto-Germanic *pusōną, *pusjaną (“to snort, blow”), from *pus- (“to blow, breathe hard”), from Proto-Indo-European *bew- (“to blow, swell”). Compare Low German pusten (“to blow, puff”), German dialectal pfausen (“to sneeze, snort”), Norwegian dialectal pysa (“to blow”).

ex.en: He posed as my close friend.
ex.ja: 彼はいかにも私の親友らしく見せかけた。

ex.en: Tom was posing as a doctor.
ex.ja: トムは医者を装っていた。

ex.en: He posed as a dentist at that bar.
ex.ja: 彼はその酒場で歯医者に成りすましていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 pausare（止まる）から（後に ponere「置く」と混同された）。ある姿勢で止まる →「ポーズ（をとる）・（問題を）提起する」。

en: To cause (liquid, or liquid-like substance) to flow in a stream, either out of a container or into it.
To send out as in a stream or a flood; to cause (an emotion) to come out; to cause to escape.
The act of pouring.
Something, or an amount, poured.

pour.ety:
From Middle English pouren (“to pour”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Old Northern French purer (“to sift (grain), pour out (water)”), from Latin pūrō (“to purify”), from pūrus (“pure”). Compare Middle Dutch afpuren (“to pour off, drain”).
To pour displaced several Middle English verbs:
* schenchen, schenken (“to pour”), from Old English sċenċan (“to pour out”) and Old Norse skenkja, from Proto-Germanic *skankijaną. Compare dialectal English shink, skink.
* yeten, from Old English ġēotan (“to pour”), from Proto-Germanic *geutaną.
* birlen (“to pour, serve drink to”), from Old English byrel

ex.en: The excited crowd poured out of the stadium.
ex.ja: 興奮した群衆が競技場から溢れ出てきた。

ex.en: She poured a cup of tea for me.
ex.ja: 彼女は私にお茶を１杯入れてくれた。

ex.en: Words of abuse poured from his lips.
ex.ja: ののしりの言葉が彼の口をついて出てきた。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「どっと注ぐ」。→「注ぐ・（雨が）激しく降る・どっと流れ出る」。

en: To issue (something, such as printed work) for distribution and/or sale.
To announce to the public.

publish.ety: From Middle English publicen (by analogy with banish, finish), from Old French publier, from Latin publicare (“to make public, show or tell to the people, make known, declare, also (and earlier) confiscate for public use”), from publicus (“pertaining to the people, public”); see public.

ex.en: Professor White published his first book last year.
ex.ja: ホワイト教授は去年処女作を出版した。

ex.en: This local newspaper is published once a week.
ex.ja: この地方新聞は週に１回発行される。

ex.en: The magazine Look is no longer being published.
ex.ja: Ｌｏｏｋは廃刊になった。

note.ja: ラテン語 publicare（公にする）から。publ（人々の）。人々に公開する →「出版する・公表する」。

en: Wholly; really, completely.
Solely; exclusively; merely, simply.

purely.ety: From Middle English purely, equivalent to pure + -ly.

ex.en: I only found out about it purely by accident.
ex.ja: 私がそれに気づいたのはほんの偶然に過ぎません。

ex.en: He met Sam purely by chance.
ex.ja: 彼はサミーにまったく偶然に会った。

ex.en: Is he someone who is interested in a purely sexual relationship?
ex.ja: 彼はヤリ目なのでしょうか。

note.ja: pure（純粋な）+ -ly。「純粋に・まったく」。

en: Something that is rented.
The payment made to rent something.
Relating to rent.
Relating to renting.

ex.ja: この店はレンタルビデオ店です。

ex.ja: これはレンタカーです。

ex.en: It's a rental car.
ex.ja: レンタカーなのよ。

note.ja: render（返す・与える）の仲間 rent（賃貸料）+ al。→「賃貸（の）・レンタル」。

en: As it appears; apparently.
In a seemly manner; decorously; with propriety.

seemingly.ety: From Middle English semyngly, equivalent to seeming + -ly.

note.ja: seeming（見せかけの）+ -ly。seem（〜に見える）。「一見したところ」。

en: In a severe manner; with severity.

severely.ety:

English -ly

From severe + -ly.

ex.en: I found a bird whose wing was severely damaged.
ex.ja: 羽に深い傷を負った小鳥を見つけました。

ex.en: It is impossible to speak too severely of his conduct.
ex.ja: 彼の行為はいかにきびしく責めてもしすぎるということはない。

ex.en: It is severely cold this winter.
ex.ja: 今年の冬は寒さが厳しいですね。

note.ja: severe（厳しい）+ -ly。「ひどく」。

en: Any predatory fish of the superorder Selachimorpha, with a cartilaginous skeleton and 5 to 7 gill slits on each side of its head.
Meat of this animal, consumed as food.

shark.ety:
From Middle English shark (used by Thomas Beckington in 1442 to refer to a kind of fish), of uncertain origin. Most likely from a semantic extension of the German-derived shark (“scoundrel”), see below. The fish was originally called a dogfish or haye in English and Middle English. Its name in Old English is unknown, although some uses of the word hranfisċ that do not appear to carry the sense of "whale" may have been referencing it.
alternative theories
Some older dictionaries derived the word from Latin c(h)archarias, c(h)acharus (from Ancient Greek), but admit that "the requisite [Old Frenc

ex.en: According to the news, he was eaten by sharks.
ex.ja: ニュースによると彼はサメに食べられたということだ。

ex.en: My older brother borrowed money from a loan shark.
ex.ja: 兄が高利貸しに借金したんです。

ex.en: Tom caught a shark.
ex.ja: トムはサメを捕まえた。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。→「サメ・強欲な人（loan shark 高利貸し）」。

en: The intercardinal compass point halfway between south and west; specifically at a bearing of 225°.
Of, in or pertaining to the southwest; southwestern.
Situated toward or in the direction of the southwest; southwestward; southwesterly.
Towards or in the direction of the southwest; southwestwards.

southwest.ety: From Middle English southwest, southewest, from Old English sūþwest and sūþanwestan, equivalent to south + west. Cognate with West Frisian súdwest, Dutch zuidwest, German Südwesten, Danish sydvest, Swedish sydväst.

note.ja: south + west。「南西」。

zh: 故人之親友 /故人之亲友

en: One who survives, especially one who survives a traumatic experience.
A person who is able to endure hardship.

survivor.ety:

ex.ja: 生存者を求めて彼らはあちこちをさがし回った。

ex.en: The sole survivor of the crash was a baby.
ex.ja: その墜落事故の唯一の生存者は赤ちゃんだった。

note.ja: sur（越えて）+ viv（生きる）+ or（人）。生き延びた人 →「生存者」。

en: Based on precise facts, which, however, may be contrary to common belief or casual terminology.
Based on formal (de jure) arguments, which, however, may be misleading.

technically.ety:

ex.ja: 規則の上では彼はまだ学生だ。

ex.ja: これらの作業は技術的に不可能である。

ex.en: The cochlea implant is a technically ingenious device.
ex.ja: 人工内耳は技術的に巧妙な機器です。

note.ja: technical（技術的な）+ -ly。「技術的に」→「厳密に言えば」。

en: Limitless or without bounds; unrestricted.

unlimited.ety: From Middle English unlimitid, equivalent to un- + limited.

note.ja: un（否定）+ limited（制限された）。ラテン語 limes（境界）。「無制限の」。limit と同じ。

en: Nervous and worried.
Having a feeling of anxiety or disquietude; extremely concerned, especially about something that will happen in the future or that is unk…

Borrowed from Latin anxius, from angō (“to cause pain, choke”); akin to Ancient Greek ἄγχω (ánkhō, “to choke”). See anger; angst. The suffix has been influenced by unrelated -ous.

ex.en: Everybody was anxious to know what had happened.
ex.ja: 何事が起こったのか誰もが知りたがっていた。

ex.en: I am anxious to visit Britain once again.
ex.ja: もう一度イギリスを訪れたいと思っている。

ex.en: Chris is very anxious to go to college.
ex.ja: クリスはとても大学に行きたがっている。

note.ja: ラテン語 anxius（締めつけられた）から。angere（締めつける）。anger、anguish と同じ祖先 →「心配して・切望して」。

en: A convenience store, originally one that sold coffee and similar basic items.

ex.en: That cafe has a pretty good breakfast special.
ex.ja: あの喫茶店のモーニングサービス結構いけるよ。

ex.en: Turn left and you will find the cafe.
ex.ja: 左へ曲がれば、喫茶店が見つかるでしょう。

ex.en: We had a quick lunch at a cafe.
ex.ja: 私達は喫茶店で素早い昼食を食べた。

note.ja: フランス語 café（コーヒー）から。コーヒーを出す店 →「カフェ」。coffee と同じ語源。

ex.ja: 私はたばこを買いに行かされた。

ex.en: Someone left a burning cigarette on the table.
ex.ja: 誰かがこのテーブルに火が付いたままのタバコをおきっぱなしにしました。

ex.en: I stopped so I could smoke a cigarette.
ex.ja: 私はタバコを吸うために立ち止まった。

note.ja: スペイン語 cigarro（葉巻）にフランス語の縮小辞 -ette がついた語 →「紙巻きたばこ」。

en: The veneration, devotion, and religious rites given to a deity (especially in a historical polytheistic context), or (in a Christian cont…
A group of people having an obsession with or intense admiration for a particular activity, idea, person or thing.
Of or relating to a cult.
Enjoyed by a small, loyal group.

cult.ety: Derived from French culte, from Latin cultus (“care, adoration; cult”), from colō (“cultivate; protect”).

ex.en: Is it true that Tom joined a cult?
ex.ja: トムがカルト集団に入ったって、本当？

ex.en: What's the difference between a religion and a cult?
ex.ja: 宗教とカルトの違いは何ですか？

ex.en: Is it true Tom joined a cult?
ex.ja: トムがカルト集団に入ったって、本当？

note.ja: ラテン語 cultus（崇拝・耕作）から。cult（耕す・あがめる）。→「崇拝・カルト」。culture と同じ語源。

en: (also dairy products or dairy produce) Products produced from milk.
A place, often on a farm, where milk is processed and turned into products such as butter and cheese.
Referring to products produced from milk.
Referring to products produced from animal milk as opposed to non-milk substitutes.

dairy.ety: Inherited from Middle English deyerie (“dairy, dairy farm”), from Anglo-Norman deyerie (“dairy”), from deye (“dairymaid”) + -erie (“-ery”); by surface analysis, dey (“dairymaid”) + -ry. Cognate with Scots dery, dyrie.

ex.en: I really hate dairy products.
ex.ja: 私は本当に乳製品が嫌いです。

ex.en: A dairy cow is a useful animal.
ex.ja: 乳牛というのは、役に立つ動物です。

ex.en: I seldom eat dairy products.
ex.ja: 乳製品はめったに食べません。

note.ja: 古英語 dǣge（パンをこねる女性）＋ -ry。lady の -dy と同じ語源 →「乳製品・酪農場」。

en: Often used as an affectionate term of address: a person who is very dear to one.
A person who is kind, sweet, etc., and thus lovable; a pet, a sweetheart; also, an animal or thing which is cute and lovable.
Very dear; beloved, cherished, favourite.
Very cute or lovable; adorable, charming, sweet.
To call (someone) "darling" (noun sense 1).

darling.ety: The noun is derived from Middle English dereling, derelyng (“beloved person; beloved of God, devout Christian”), from Old English dīerling, dēorling (“favourite, darling; minion”), from Proto-West Germanic *diuriling, from Proto-Germanic *diurijalingaz, from *diurijaz (“beloved, dear; expensive”) (further etymology uncertain, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“hot, warm; to burn”), or *dweh₂- (“distant, long; to remove, separate”)) + *-ilingaz (suffix forming (diminutive) nouns with the sense of ‘belonging to; coming from’). By surface analysis, dear + -ling (suffix meaning ‘immature

ex.en: What are you doing, darling?
ex.ja: 何をしているの、ダーリン？

ex.en: Let's dance, my darling.
ex.ja: ねぇ、あなた、踊りましょう。

ex.en: I call my sweetheart darling.
ex.ja: 私は恋人を「ダーリン」と呼びます。

note.ja: 古英語 dēorling ＝ dear（大切な）+ -ling（小さいもの）。「最愛の人」。

en: Joy; pleasure.
Something that gives great joy or pleasure.
To give delight to; to affect with great pleasure; to please highly.
To have or take great pleasure.

delight.ety: Attested from the 13th century, from Middle English delite, from Old French deleiter, deliter, from Latin dēlectāre (“to delight, please”), frequentative of dēlicere (“to allure, entice”), from dē- (“away”) + laciō (“to lure, to deceive”), from Proto-Italic *lakjō (“to draw, pull”), of unknown ultimate origin. Doublet of delect. Related with delectation, delicate, delicious and dilettante. The modern unetymological spelling (instead of expected delite) is influenced by light and other words ending in -ight, such as might, bright, etc. The -gh- may also be an attempt to represent the Latin -c-;

ex.en: I read your new book with real delight.
ex.ja: 新しい本を本当に大喜びで読ませていただきました。

ex.en: Great was our delight when we won the game.
ex.ja: その試合に勝った時、私たちの喜びは大きかった。

ex.en: To my great delight, he won the first prize.
ex.ja: 私がたいへんうれしかったことに彼は一等賞をとった。

note.ja: ラテン語 delectare（魅了する）から。light（光）の影響で gh が入った →「大喜び・喜ばせる」。

en: A daily log of experiences, especially those of the writer.
A personal organizer or appointment diary.
To keep a diary or journal.

diary.ety: From Latin diārium (“a daily allowance for soldiers, in Late Latin also ‘diary’”), neuter of *diārius, from diēs (“a day”) (whence also journal). Cognate with Spanish diario (“daily; diary”).

ex.en: Have you written in your diary yet today?
ex.ja: 今日の日記はもう書きましたか。

ex.en: Did you write anything in your diary today?
ex.ja: 今日は日記を付けましたか。

ex.en: I read a lot in my diary yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日たくさん日記を読みました。

note.ja: ラテン語 dies（日）から。daily な記録 →「日記」。dairy（乳製品）と綴りが似ているので注意。

en: To fail to agree; to have a different opinion or belief.
To fail to conform or correspond with.

disagree.ety: From Middle English disagre (“to refuse to assent to”), from Anglo-Norman disagreer, disagrer, desagreer (“to refuse assent”), from Old French desagreer, desagrëer (“to be disagreeable; to be unpleasant”) (modern French désagréer (“to displease”)); the English word is analysable as dis- + agree.

ex.en: This is where we absolutely disagree with you.
ex.ja: この点で私達はまったくあなたと意見が違います。

ex.en: This is where I absolutely disagree with you.
ex.ja: この点では、私は全くあなたと意見が違う。

ex.en: This is the reason I disagree with you.
ex.ja: こういうわけで私はあなたに反対なのです。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ agree（同意する）。「意見が合わない」。

en: To create (a hole) by removing material with a drill (tool).
To practice, especially in (or as in) a military context.
A tool or machine used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.
The portion of a drilling tool that drives the bit.

drill.ety: From Middle Dutch drillen (“bore, move in a circle”).

ex.en: We had a fire drill at school today.
ex.ja: 今日、学校で避難訓練をしました。

ex.en: We had a fire drill yesterday.
ex.ja: 私たちは昨日防火訓練をした。

ex.en: They intended to drill for oil.
ex.ja: 彼らは穴をあけて石油を掘り当てようとした。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 drillen（穴をあける・回す）から。「錐」→ 繰り返し回すような「訓練」。

en: The currency unit of the European Monetary Union. Symbol: €
A coin with a face value of one euro.

euro.ety: The name euro was the winner of a contest open to the general public to propose names for the new European currency, and as such is technically a neologism, although it obviously alludes to the common root of geographical names for the continent Europe, derived from Latin Europa, from Ancient Greek Εὐρώπη (Eurṓpē), the name in Greek mythology of a princess, abducted by Zeus as a bull across the Bosporus. According to the official story, the term was coined by Belgian teacher and esperantist Germain Pirlot in 1995, who suggested it in a letter to Jacques Santer, then President of the European C

ex.en: How much is 300 euros in U.S. dollars?
ex.ja: 300ユーロって、アメリカドルでいくらなの？

ex.en: I don't remember exactly, but I spent over 1000 euros.
ex.ja: 正確には覚えてないんだけど、1,000ユーロ以上使ったよ。

ex.en: They cost three Euros a piece.
ex.ja: 1つ3ユーロです。

note.ja: Europe の短縮。1999年に導入された通貨。

en: To move (something) in regular procession through a system.
To change or transform (something).

evolve.ety: Borrowed from Latin ēvolvō (“unroll, unfold”), from ē- (“out of”) (short form of ex) + volvō (“roll”).

ex.en: What kinds of animals will evolve from us?
ex.ja: 私たちが進化したらどんな種の動物になるだろうか。

ex.en: The situation has evolved into a more complex problem.
ex.ja: 事態はさらに複雑な問題に発展した。

ex.en: A concrete plan evolved after much discussion.
ex.ja: 十分に議論したあとで具体的な計画が進展した。

note.ja: ラテン語 evolvere ＝ e（外へ）+ volvere（転がす）。「巻物を広げる」→「展開する・進化する」。revolve と同じ volv。

en: To estimate how something will be in the future.
To foreshadow; to suggest something in advance.
An estimation of a future condition.
A prediction of the weather.

forecast.ety:
From Middle English forecasten, forcasten, equivalent to fore- + cast.
The noun is from Middle English forecast, forcast.

ex.en: According to the weather forecast, it'll snow tomorrow.
ex.ja: 天気予報によればあすは雪だ。

ex.en: According to the weather forecast, it'll rain tomorrow.
ex.ja: 天気予報によると、明日は雨だそうだ。

ex.en: The weather forecast said it's going to rain.
ex.ja: 天気予報だと、雨が降るって。

note.ja: fore（前もって）+ cast（投げる）。前もって（予測を）投げる →「予報・予測する」。

en: The process, or the power, of governing; government or administration.
The specific system by which a political system is ruled.

governance.ety: From Middle English governaunce, from Old French gouvernance, governance, equivalent to govern + -ance.

ex.en: Corporate governance and accountability are being strengthened.
ex.ja: コーポレートガバナンスや説明責任を強化している。

note.ja: ラテン語 gubernare（舵を取る）から。→「統治・管理・ガバナンス」。

en: A close embrace, especially when charged with an emotion such as affection, joy, relief, lust, anger, aggression, compassion, or the like…
A particular grip in wrestling.
To cling closely together.
To embrace by holding closely, especially in the arms.

hug.ety: From earlier hugge (“to embrace, clasp with the arms”) (1560), probably representing a conflation of huck (“to crouch, huddle down”) and Old Norse hugga (“to comfort, console”), from hugr (“mind, heart, thought”), from Proto-Germanic *hugiz (“mind, thought, sense”), cognate with Icelandic hugga (“to comfort”), Old English hyġe (“thought”) (whence high (Etymology 2)).

ex.en: Tom and Mary are hugging each other naked.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは生まれたままの姿で抱き合っている。

ex.en: Would it be OK if I hugged you?
ex.ja: 抱き締めてもいいですか？

ex.en: She hugged the baby to her breast.
ex.ja: 彼女は赤ん坊を腕に抱きしめた。

note.ja: 古ノルド語 hugga（慰める）から。→「抱きしめる・抱擁」。

en: Used to mark a statement as having importance.
In an important manner.

Etymology tree
English important
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English importantly
From important + -ly.

ex.ja: 可愛い。そして何より品がいい。

ex.en: The rules must be few and, more importantly, simple.
ex.ja: 規則は少なく、さらに重要なことには、簡単でなければならない。

ex.en: She's cute, and more importantly, has class.
ex.ja: 可愛い。そして何より品がいい。

note.ja: important + -ly。「重要なことに」。

en: Situated in, or designed to be used in, or carried on within, the interior of a building.

ex.ja: 世界一の大きさを誇る室内ビーチは、ドイツのブランデンブルクにあります。

ex.en: Nancy enjoys indoor games.
ex.ja: ナンシーは屋内競技が好きです。

note.ja: in（中の）+ door（戸）。「屋内の」。outdoor の対。

en: Having or exerting influence.
A person who has influence

influential.ety: From Medieval Latin īnfluentiālis, from īnfluentia + -ālis. By surface analysis, influence + -ial.

ex.en: I'm not as influential as you think I am.
ex.ja: あなたが思っているほど私は影響力がない。

ex.en: He's very influential in Kansai's adult industry.
ex.ja: 彼は関西のアダルト産業に強い影響力を持っている。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ flu（流れる）+ ential。影響（influence）を流し込む →「影響力のある」。

en: Unable to be seen; out of sight; not visible.
Not appearing on the surface.
To make invisible, to invisiblize.

invisible.ety:
From Middle English invisible, from Old French invisible, from Late Latin invīsibilis. Displaced native Old English unġesewenlīċ.
Morphologically in- + visible. Piecewise doublet of unvisible.

ex.en: Tom said he saw the invisible man today.
ex.ja: トムが今日透明人間を見たんだって。

ex.en: Tom said that he saw the invisible man today.
ex.ja: トムが今日透明人間を見たんだって。

ex.en: Can you see the invisible man?
ex.ja: 透明人間が見えますか？

note.ja: in（否定）+ vis（見る）+ ible。見えない →「目に見えない」。

en: A pair of trousers made from denim cotton.

jeans.ety: From Gene(s) (also spelled Jean(s)), an obsolete English name for the Italian city of Genoa. Compare French Gênes. In the context of clothing, the term originally denoted a kind of coarse cotton (known more fully as Gene(s) fustian) that was associated with Genoa. It began to be used for trousers made of such cloth in the 19th century. At this point, the final -s was reanalysed as a plural ending.

ex.en: Is it OK if I go in jeans?
ex.ja: ジーンズで行ってもいいかな？

ex.en: Made in Italy, these jeans were very expensive.
ex.ja: イタリー製なので、このジーンズはとても値段が高かった。

ex.en: My brother gave me a pair of jeans.
ex.ja: 兄は私にジーパンをくれた。

note.ja: イタリアの港町ジェノバ（Genoa、フランス語 Gênes）で作られた丈夫な布から →「ジーンズ」。

en: In civil law, a case where two or more people disagree and one or more of the parties take the case to a court for resolution.
To bring a lawsuit.

ex.en: I would prefer any alternative to a lawsuit.
ex.ja: 私は訴訟に変わるものがあればなんでもいい。

ex.en: The lawsuit is likely to end in our defeat.
ex.ja: 裁判はこちらの負けにおわりそうだ。

ex.en: The lawsuit remains undecided.
ex.ja: 訴訟は未決である。

note.ja: law（法）+ suit（訴訟）。→「訴訟」。suit は sequi（追う）から。

en: A crack, crevice, fissure, or hole which admits water or other fluid, or lets it escape.
The entrance or escape of a fluid through a crack, fissure, or other aperture.
To allow fluid or gas to pass through an opening that should be sealed.
(of a fluid or gas) To pass through an opening that should be sealed.

leak.ety:
From Middle English leken (“to let water in or out”), from Old English *lecan (“to leak”), Middle Dutch leken (“to leak, drip”) or Old Norse leka (“to leak, drip”); all from Proto-Germanic *lekaną (“to leak, drain”), from Proto-Indo-European *leg- (“to leak”).
Cognate with Dutch lekken (“to leak”), German lechen, lecken (“to leak”), Danish lække (“to leak”), Swedish läcka (“to leak”), Norwegian Bokmål lekke (“to leak”), Faroese, Icelandic, and Norwegian Nynorsk leka (“to leak”). Related also to Old English leċċan (“to water, wet”), Albanian lag, lak (“to damp, make wet”). See also leach, lake.

ex.en: Tom is taking a leak behind the house.
ex.ja: トムは家の後ろでおしっこしてるんだ。

ex.en: There is a leak in the roof.
ex.ja: この屋根は雨漏りがする。

ex.en: The information seems to have leaked out.
ex.ja: 情報が外部に漏れたらしい。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 leken（滴る）から。「漏れる」→ 情報を「漏らす」。

en: A composer, conductor, or performer of music; specifically, a person who sings and/or plays a musical instrument as a hobby, occupation, …

musician.ety: From Middle English musician, musicien, from Old French musicien (“musician”), equivalent to musike + -ien. By surface analysis, music + -ician.

ex.en: A musician can appreciate small differences in sounds.
ex.ja: 音楽家は音の小さな違いが分かる。

ex.en: I am the first musician in my family.
ex.ja: 私は家族の中で初めての音楽家なのです。

ex.en: I know that he is a famous musician.
ex.ja: 私は彼が有名な音楽家であることを知っている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mousikē（ミューズの技）から。music（音楽）+ ian（人）→「音楽家」。

en: A tree of species Olea europaea cultivated since ancient times in the Mediterranean for its fruit and the oil obtained from it.
The small oval fruit of this tree, eaten ripe (usually black) or unripe (usually green).
Of a grayish green color, that of an unripe olive.

olive.ety: From Middle English olyve, from Old French olive (“olive, olive tree”), from Latin olīva (“olive”), itself from either Etruscan *𐌄𐌋𐌄𐌉𐌅𐌀 (*eleiva), Proto-Hellenic *elaíwā (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀨𐀷 (e-ra-wa), Ancient Greek ἐλαίᾱ (elaíā)), or the same source as those two. In any case, ultimately from a Mediterranean Pre-Greek source, possibly Proto-Berber *wlw (“wild olive”). More questionably, maybe from Proto-Indo-European *loiwom (compare Old Church Slavonic лои (loi, “tallow”), Old Armenian եւղ (ewł, “oil”)). Doublet of oliva and oil. Displaced native Old English eleberġe, literally "oil b

ex.en: I'd rather use olive oil than butter.
ex.ja: バターを使うよりオリーブオイルの方がいいな。

ex.en: We'd like to order 18 tonnes of olive oil.
ex.ja: オリーブオイルを１８ＭＴ注文します。

ex.en: You like olives, don't you?
ex.ja: オリーブが好きなんだよね？

note.ja: ギリシャ語 elaia（オリーブ）から。oil（油）と同じ。→「オリーブ・オリーブ色」。

en: Given to strong feeling, sometimes romantic, sexual, or both.
Fired with intense feeling.

passionate.ety: From Middle English passionat, from Medieval Latin passiōnātus (“affected, impassioned, libidinous, easely angered”). Equivalent to passion + -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Compare French passionné.

ex.en: She had a passionate interest in music.
ex.ja: 彼女は音楽を熱烈に愛好していた。

ex.en: So passionate was his letter that she was moved to tears.
ex.ja: 彼の手紙がとても情熱的だったので彼女は感動して涙がでできた。

ex.en: Tom is passionate about music.
ex.ja: トムは、音楽に情熱を注いでいます。

note.ja: ラテン語 pati（苦しむ）から。passion（情熱）+ ate。→「情熱的な」。

en: An official whose job is to receive taxes or other monies; a tax collector, a treasurer.
A person who receives something in a general sense; a recipient.

receiver.ety: Inherited from Middle English receyvour, from Anglo-Norman receverre, receivour et al., later also reformed as receive + -er. Compare recevor, rescaivour.

ex.en: I put the receiver to my ear.
ex.ja: 私は受話器を耳に当てた。

ex.en: He took up the receiver and dialed.
ex.ja: 彼は受話器を取り上げてダイアルを回した。

ex.en: I forgot to lift the receiver before dialing the number.
ex.ja: ぼくはうっかり受話器をはずさないでダイヤルを回した。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ ceiv（取る）+ er。受け取るもの →「受話器・受信機・受取人」。

en: A tumultuous disturbance of the public peace by a large group of people, often involving violence or damage to property.
A wide and unconstrained variety.
To create or take part in a riot; to raise an uproar or sedition.
To cause to riot; to throw into a tumult.

riot.ety:
From Middle English riot (“debauched living, dissipation”), from Old French riote (“debate”), from rioter (“to quarrel”), perhaps related to riboter or from Latin rugio (“to roar”).
Compare French riotte and Occitan riòta.

ex.en: The riot police arrived on the scene.
ex.ja: 機動隊が現場に到着した。

ex.en: The riot was soon put down by the police.
ex.ja: その暴動はすぐに警察によって鎮圧された。

ex.en: Big cities have too high a potential for riots.
ex.ja: 大都市では騒動が起こる可能性が大変大きい。

note.ja: 古フランス語 riote（口論・騒ぎ）から。→「暴動・大騒ぎ」。

en: A list of individuals or groups, usually for an organization of some kind such as military officers and enlisted personnel enrolled in a …
A list of the jobs to be performed by members of an organization and often with the date and time that they are expected to perform them.
To place the name of (a person) on a roster.
To show the elements of a set by listing them inside brackets.

roster.ety: Borrowed from Dutch rooster (“gridiron, table, list”), from Middle Dutch roosten (“to roast”). More at roast.

note.ja: オランダ語 rooster（焼き網・リスト）から。表の格子が焼き網に似ていたことから。「名簿・勤務表」。

en: One who is hired to perform regular household or other duties, and receives compensation. As opposed to a slave.
One who serves another, providing help in some manner.

servant.ety: From Middle English servaunt, from Old French servant, from the present participle of the verb servir. Doublet of sergeant and servient. Morphologically serve + -ant. Displaced native Old English þeġn.

ex.en: He had three servants to wait on him.
ex.ja: 彼には彼に仕える召し使いが３人いた。

ex.en: He was a kind master to his servants.
ex.ja: 彼は使用人に優しい雇い主だった。

ex.en: He is rich enough to keep a servant.
ex.ja: 彼は召し使いをおけるほど金持ちだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 servire（仕える）から。serv + ant（人）。→「召使い・使用人・公務員（civil servant）」。

en: Equipment designed for a particular purpose; an apparatus.
The fashion in which something is organized or arranged.

note.ja: set up（組み立てる）の名詞化。「準備・仕組み・設定」→（俗）「わな」。

en: The main bones of the head considered as a unit; including the cranium, facial bones, and mandible.
These bones as a symbol for death; death's-head.
To hit in the head with a fist, a weapon, or a thrown object.
To strike the top of (the ball).

skull.ety:
From Middle English sculle, scolle (also schulle, scholle), probably from a dialectal form of Old Norse skalli (“bald head, skull”), itself probably related to Old English sċealu (“husk”), to Proto-Norse *ᛋᚲᚨᛚᛟ (*skalo), from Proto-Germanic *skallô; compare Finnish kallo. Compare Scots scull, Danish skal (“skull”) and skalle (“bald head, skull”), Norwegian skalle, Swedish skalle and especially dialectal Swedish skulle.
Related to Old Norse skoltr (“brow”), skolptr (“muzzle, snout”), akin to Icelandic skoltur (“jaw”), dialectal Swedish skult, skulle (“dome, crown of the head, skull”), Norwegian

ex.en: Closer examination revealed that the skull had been crushed by some heavy blow.
ex.ja: 調べを進めるうちに、頭蓋骨が、何か重い一撃を受けて打ち砕かれているのが明らかになった。

note.ja: 古ノルド語 skalli（はげ頭）から。→「頭蓋骨」。

en: The sound of a violent impact; a violent striking together.
A traffic collision.
To break (something brittle) violently.
To be destroyed by being smashed.

smash.ety: Uncertain, probably of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Swedish smask (“to smack with the lips”), dialectal Swedish smaska (“to smack, kiss”), Danish smaske (“to smack with the lips”), Low German smaksen (“to smack with the lips, kiss”).

ex.en: Who smashed the window? Tell me the truth.
ex.ja: 誰が窓を割ったの？本当のことを言いなさい。

ex.en: There was a smash-up out on Route 66 today.
ex.ja: 今日ルート６６で衝突事故があったんだ。

ex.en: The bottle smashed to pieces.
ex.ja: 瓶は粉々に割れた。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。smack（ピシャリ）+ mash（つぶす）とされる。「粉々に砕く」→「大ヒット」。

en: A three-dimensional work of art, usually representing a person or animal, usually created by sculpting, carving, molding, or casting.
To form a statue of; to make into a statue.

statue.ety: From Old French statue, from Latin statua, derived from statuō (“set up or erect”). Doublet of statua.

ex.en: This statue is as large as life.
ex.ja: この像は実物大です。

ex.en: We must move this statue very carefully.
ex.ja: 私たちは十分注意してこの彫像を動かさなければならない。

ex.en: He was as still as a statue.
ex.ja: 彼は彫像のようにじっとしていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 statua（立てられたもの）から。sta（立つ）。立っている像 →「像・彫像」。

en: In a way that causes surprise because it is unexpected, or unusual.

surprisingly.ety:
Etymology tree
English surprising
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English surprisingly
From surprising + -ly.

ex.en: Tom always gets the job done surprisingly fast.
ex.ja: トムはいつも驚くほど仕事が早い。

ex.en: The stock market was surprisingly quiet today.
ex.ja: 株式市場は今日は驚くべき動きはなかった。

ex.en: This book is surprisingly easy to read, isn't it?
ex.ja: 案外、この本は読みやすいね。

note.ja: surprising（驚くべき）+ -ly。surprise は sur（上から）+ prendre（つかむ）。「不意につかまえる」。

en: To give up into the power, control, or possession of another.
To yield (a town, a fortification, etc.) to an enemy.
An act of surrendering, submission into the possession of another; a feeling of abandonment and resignation; the deliberate cessation of …
The yielding or delivery of a possession in response to a demand.

surrender.ety: From Middle English surrendren, from Old French surrendre, from sur- + rendre (“render”). Displaced native Old English on hand gān.

ex.en: The soldiers were told never to surrender.
ex.ja: 兵士たちは決して降伏しないように言われた。

ex.en: If I had to surrender, I'd rather choose death.
ex.ja: 降伏するくらいなら死を選びます。

ex.en: Under the circumstances we have no choice but to surrender.
ex.ja: 現状では、私たちは降参するしかない。

note.ja: sur（上に）+ render（与える・返す）。（すべてを）引き渡す →「降伏する・引き渡す」。

en: Arousing suspicion.
Distrustful or tending to suspect.

suspicious.ety: From Old French sospecious, from Latin suspiciosus, suspitiosus.

ex.en: The police are suspicious of the old man.
ex.ja: 警察はその老人を疑っている。

ex.en: The way she spoke to us was suspicious.
ex.ja: 彼女の私達への口のきき方は疑い深げだった。

ex.en: She said that she saw a suspicious man.
ex.ja: 彼女は怪しい男を見たと言いました。

note.ja: su（下から）+ spic（見る）+ ious。下から疑いの目で見る →「疑わしい・疑い深い」。suspect（疑う）。

en: A person between thirteen and nineteen years old (inclusive).

teenager.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *déḱm̥
Proto-Germanic *tehun
Proto-West Germanic *tehunder.
Anglian Old English -tēne
Middle English -tene
English -teen
Proto-Indo-European *h₂ey-
Proto-Indo-European *-u
Proto-Indo-European *h₂óyu
Proto-Indo-European *-wom
Proto-Indo-European *h₂oywom
Proto-Italic *aiwom
Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-ts
Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂ts
Proto-Italic *-tāts
Proto-Italic *aiwotāts
Latin aetātem
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂tos
Proto-Italic *-ātos
Latin -ātus
Proto-Indo-Euro

ex.en: Teenagers want to be independent of their parents.
ex.ja: 十代の子供たちは親から独立したいと思っている。

ex.en: A teenager sometimes acts like a baby.
ex.ja: ティーンエイジャーはたまに赤ん坊のような行動をとる。

ex.en: The report revealed that many teenagers are alcoholics.
ex.ja: その報告書から１０代の多くの子供がアルコール中毒にかかっていることが分かった。

note.ja: teenage（10代の）+ -er。「10代の若者」。

en: Sensitive or painful to the touch.
Easily bruised or injured; not firm or hard; delicate.
The inner flight muscle (pectoralis minor) of poultry.
tenderly
To work on a tender.

tender.ety: From Middle English tender, tendere, from Anglo-Norman tendre, Old French tendre, from Latin tener, tenerum (“soft, delicate”).

ex.en: Tom passed away at the tender age of 30.
ex.ja: トムは享年３０という若さでこの世を去った。

ex.en: His voice was full of tender concern.
ex.ja: 彼の声には優しい気づかいが満ちていた。

ex.en: What a tender heart she has.
ex.ja: 彼女はなんと優しい心の持ち主なのだろう。

note.ja: 「優しい・柔らかい」はラテン語 tener（柔らかい）から、「入札する」は tendere（差し出す）から来た別語。

en: In a thorough or complete manner.

ex.en: If you learn English at all, learn it thoroughly.
ex.ja: どうせ英語をやるのなら徹底的にやれ。

ex.en: We went over the house thoroughly before buying it.
ex.ja: その家を徹底的に調べてから購入した。

ex.en: He is thoroughly familiar with the business.
ex.ja: 彼はその仕事に精通している。

note.ja: thorough（徹底的な）+ -ly。thorough は through の古い形で「最後まで通した」。

en: A region of space that contains no matter.
The condition of rarefaction, or reduction of pressure below that of the atmosphere, in a vessel, such as the condenser of a steam engine…
To clean (something) with a vacuum cleaner.
To use a vacuum cleaner.

vacuum.ety:
Borrowed from New Latin vacuum (“vacuum”), a subsense of Classical Latin vacuum (“empty space”), a substantivised form of vacuus (“empty”); related to vacāre (“to be empty”).
The exercise sense comes from analogy to the sucking action of a vacuum cleaner.

ex.en: For that experiment they need a complete vacuum.
ex.ja: その実験には真空が必要だ。

ex.en: His death has left a vacuum in their lives.
ex.ja: 彼の死は彼らの生活に空しさをもたらした。

ex.en: I need to vacuum the car.
ex.ja: 車に掃除機かけなきゃ。

note.ja: ラテン語 vacuus（空の）から。vac（空）。空っぽの空間 →「真空・電気掃除機（で掃除する）」。

en: The act of varying; a partial change in the form, position, state, or qualities of a thing.
A related but distinct thing.

variation.ety: From Middle French variation, from Old French variacion, from Latin variātiō, from vary + -ation.

ex.en: Obviously there are many variations between these two extremes.
ex.ja: むろん、この両極端の間に多くのバリエーションがある。

ex.en: The reason for this is that we found no variation of those morphemes.
ex.ja: このことの理由は、それらの形態素に変異形がまったく見出されなかったからである。

note.ja: ラテン語 variare（変える）から。→「変化・変動・変奏曲」。

en: An assertion, especially an accusation, not necessarily based on facts.
The act of alleging.

allegation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French allégation, from Latin allegatio, from allegare. By surface analysis, allege + -ation, see allege.

note.ja: ラテン語 allegare（申し立てる）から。証拠のない申し立て →「（裏付けのない）主張・申し立て」。

en: To act before (someone), especially to prevent an action.
To take up or introduce (something) prematurely.

anticipate.ety: Borrowed from Latin anticipātus, perfect passive participle of anticipō (“to anticipate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ante- (“before”), + capiō (“to take”, cip- when prefixed) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). See capable.

ex.en: I anticipated a quiet vacation in the mountains.
ex.ja: 山で静かな休日を過ごせるものと楽しみにしていた。

ex.en: We didn't anticipate their buying a new car.
ex.ja: 私たちは彼らが新車を買うなんて予想もしなかった。

ex.en: He anticipates that he will be in trouble.
ex.ja: 彼は困ったことになるだろうと予想している。

note.ja: anti（= ante 前に）+ cip（取る）+ ate。前もって取る →「予期する・先回りする」。

en: A professional who designs buildings or other structures, or who prepares plans and superintends construction.
A person who plans, devises or contrives the achievement of a desired result.
To design, plan, or orchestrate.

architect.ety: From Middle French architecte, from Latin architectus, from Ancient Greek ἀρχιτέκτων (arkhitéktōn, “master builder”), from ἀρχι- (arkhi-, “chief”) + τέκτων (téktōn, “builder”). By surface analysis, archi- + -tect.

ex.en: The hotel was designed by a Japanese architect.
ex.ja: そのホテルは日本人の建築家によって設計された。

ex.en: Tom has a brother who is an architect.
ex.ja: トムには建築家の弟がいる。

ex.en: Tom was the architect that designed that building.
ex.ja: トムは建築士で、あの建物の設計をした。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 arkhi（主な）+ tektōn（大工）。棟梁 →「建築家・設計者」。tech（技術）と同じ祖先。

en: A wide bowl for washing, sometimes affixed to a wall.
A depression, natural or artificial, containing water.
To create a concavity or depression in.
To serve as or become a basin.

basin.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Celtic *baskis
Gaulish *baskisder.
Latin bacca
Vulgar Latin *baccinum
Old French bacinbor.
Middle English basyn
English basin
From Middle English basyn, from Old French bacin, from Vulgar Latin *baccinum (“wide bowl”).

ex.en: This district forms a basin.
ex.ja: この地方は盆地になっている。

ex.en: A student was run over by a car on Basin Street.
ex.ja: １人の生徒がベイスン通りで車にひかれた。

ex.en: The water in the basin has frozen solid.
ex.ja: 洗面器の水がかちかちに凍った。

note.ja: ラテン語 bacinus（鉢）から。→「洗面器・盆地・流域」。

en: Helpful or good to something or someone.
Receiving a benefit from something.
Something that provides a benefit.

beneficial.ety: From Late Latin beneficiālis (“beneficial”), from Latin beneficium (“benefit, favor, kindness”).

ex.en: Regular exercise is beneficial to good health.
ex.ja: 規則的な運動は健康によい。

ex.en: You should read books beneficial to you.
ex.ja: 君は自分のためになるような書物を読むべきだ。

ex.en: Your year-long stay in Germany was very beneficial, wasn't it?
ex.ja: あなたの１年間のドイツ滞在はとても有益でしたね。

note.ja: bene（よい）+ fic（する）+ ial。よいことをもたらす →「有益な・ためになる」。

en: Losing blood.
The flow or loss of blood from a damaged blood vessel.
Bloodletting.

ex.en: You'll have bleeding for a few hours.
ex.ja: ２、３時間出血が続きます。

ex.en: Something has to be done to stop the bleeding.
ex.ja: 出血を止めるためにどうにかしなければならない。

ex.en: I'm afraid that I have internal bleeding.
ex.ja: 内出血している気がするのですが。

note.ja: bleed（出血する）+ -ing。bleed は blood の動詞形。

en: To produce offspring sexually; to bear young.
To give birth to; to be the native place of.
All animals or plants of the same species or subspecies.
A race or lineage; offspring or issue.

ex.en: He is a man of birth and breeding.
ex.ja: 彼は生まれも育ちもいい人だ。

ex.en: Birth is much, breeding is more.
ex.ja: 人は氏より育ち。

ex.en: Clear water breeds no fish.
ex.ja: 水清ければ魚住まず。

note.ja: 古英語 brēdan（育てる）から。brood（ひな）と同系。「繁殖させる」→「品種」。

en: A woman in the context of her own wedding; one who is going to marry or has just been married.

ex.en: The bride was wearing a white wedding dress.
ex.ja: 新婦は白いウエディングドレスに身を包んでいた。

ex.en: The bride was wearing a pure white dress.
ex.ja: 花嫁さんは純白のドレスを身にまとっていた。

ex.en: He is father to the bride.
ex.ja: 彼が花嫁の父親です。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「花嫁」。bridegroom（花婿）の groom は本来 guma（男）。

en: A newly sprouted leaf or blossom that has not yet unfolded.
Something that has begun to develop.
To form buds.
To reproduce by splitting off buds.

bud.ety: From Middle English budde, bodde (“bud, seed pod”), from Old English *budde, from Proto-West Germanic *buʀdā, from Proto-Germanic *buzdǭ (compare archaic German Butte (“rosehip”), Swedish dialect bodd (“head”)), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”). Compare also German Low German Butte, Butt (“bud”), Dutch bot (“bud”), regional German Butz, Butzen (“seed pod; apple core”), German Low German Haagbutt ("rosehip"; Haagbudden (“rosehips”, plural)).

ex.en: The cold weather may keep the plants from budding.
ex.ja: 寒い天候のために植物は芽を出せないかもしれない。

ex.en: The buds are beginning to show signs of color.
ex.ja: つぼみがだんだん色づいてきた。

ex.en: The trees are budding early this year.
ex.ja: 今年は木の芽の出方が早い。

note.ja: 中英語 budde から。「芽・つぼみ」。buddy とは別語。

en: A manservant having charge of wines and liquors.
The chief male servant of a household who has charge of other employees, receives guests, directs the serving of meals, and performs vari…
To buttle, to dispense wines or liquors; to take the place of a butler.

butler.ety: From Middle English butler, butlere, boteler, botelere, from Old French buttiler, butiller, boteillier (“officer in charge of wine”), from Medieval Latin botellārius, equivalent to bottle + -er. Piecewise doublet of bottler.

ex.en: The butler announced Mr. and Mrs. Smith.
ex.ja: 使用人がしらは声を上げて「スミスご夫妻がおいでになりました」と告げた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 bouteillier（酒係）から。bouteille（瓶）。bottle と同じ。「執事」。

en: A humorous drawing, often with a caption, or a strip of such drawings.
A drawing satirising current public figures.
To draw a cartoon, a humorous drawing.
To make a preliminary sketch.

cartoon.ety: In British English first, from French carton (“sketch, cardboard, card”), from Italian cartone (“cardboard, carton, box”), augmentative of carta (“paper”), from Latin carta (“papyrus, paper”), from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs) (see there for further etymology). Doublet of carton and card.

ex.en: I always laugh when I read his cartoons.
ex.ja: 彼の漫画を読むと、いつも笑ってしまう。

ex.en: Under the cartoon, he wrote "Get your hot dogs!"
ex.ja: 漫画の下に「ホット・ドッグをどうぞ」と書いたのである。

ex.en: I've loved cartoons since I was little.
ex.ja: 小さい頃から、アニメが大好きだよ。

note.ja: イタリア語 cartone（厚紙）から。下絵を描いた厚紙 →「漫画・風刺画・アニメ」。carton（ボール箱）と同語源。

en: A young bird.
A young chicken.
To compress the lips and then separate them quickly, resulting in a percussive noise.

chick.ety: From Middle English chicke, chike, variation of chiken (“chicken", also "chick”), from Old English ċicen, ċycen (“chicken”). Sense of "young woman" dates to at least 1860 (compare chit (“young, pert woman”)). More at chicken.

ex.en: Let's pick up a chick.
ex.ja: 誰かをナンパしよう。

ex.en: Can you return starling chicks to their parents?
ex.ja: ムクドリのヒナを親鳥に返せますか。

ex.en: She bought a baby chick.
ex.ja: 彼女はひよこを買った。

note.ja: chicken の短縮。「ひな鳥」→（俗）若い女性。

en: Solid residue from roasting coal in a coke oven; used principally as a fuel and in the production of steel and formerly as a domestic fuel.
To produce coke from coal.
To turn into coke.

coke.ety: The origin is not certain. The OED says it is first attested in 1669. The MED has an earlier attestation in the related sense of "charcoal" in 1430: Middle English coke. This may be the same word as colk (“core”) (perhaps from the notion that coke is the core of the material left after it burning), from Old English *colc (“hole, well”), from Proto-West Germanic *kolk, from Proto-Germanic *kulukaz (“a hollow, depression”), from Proto-Indo-European *g(ʷ)el- (“to swallow, devour; gullet”). If so, cognate with Saterland Frisian Kolk (“maelstrom, depression, whirlpool”), West Frisian kolk (“maelstr

ex.en: I am just dying for a Coke right now.
ex.ja: 今すぐにコーラが飲みたいんだ。

ex.en: Has all the coke been drunk?
ex.ja: コーラはみんな飲んでしまったの。

ex.en: More than one bottle of coke was consumed.
ex.ja: コーラが１びん以上飲まれた。

note.ja: 「コーラ」は Coca-Cola の短縮。燃料の「コークス」は別語で語源不明。

en: Able to be compared (to).
Similar (to); like.
Something suitable for comparison.

comparable.ety: From Middle English comparable, from Middle French comparable, from Latin comparābilis. By surface analysis, compare + -able.

ex.en: This metal is comparable to iron in strength.
ex.ja: この金属は強度では鉄に匹敵する。

ex.en: A comparable car would cost far more in Japan.
ex.ja: これに匹敵するような車は日本ではずっと高いでしょう。

ex.en: As you know, life is comparable to a voyage.
ex.ja: ご存じのように人生は航海にたとえられる。

note.ja: com（共に）+ par（等しい）+ able。比べられる →「同等の・匹敵する」。

en: An official indicator that things will happen as planned.
A verification that something is true or has happened.

confirmation.ety:
From Middle English confirmacioun, from Old French confirmacion, from Latin cōnfirmātiō, noun of process from cōnfirmātus (“confirmed”), perfect passive participle of cōnfirmāre, from con- (“with”) + firmāre (“to firm or strengthen”).
Morphologically confirm + -ation.

ex.en: Thank you so much for the punctual confirmation.
ex.ja: 早々のご確認、誠に有難うございました。

ex.en: The confirmation hearings turned into a free-for-all.
ex.ja: 証人喚問はとんだ騒ぎになってしまいました。

ex.en: The confirmation came out.
ex.ja: 確証が出てきた。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ firm（固い）+ ation。しっかり固めること →「確認・承認」。firm（固い・会社）。

en: A stand-alone cabinet designed to stand on the floor; especially, one integrated with home entertainment equipment, such as a TV or stere…
A desk-like cabinet, table, or stand upon which controls, instruments, and displays are mounted.
To comfort (someone) in a time of grief, disappointment, etc.

console.ety:
Borrowed from French console (“bracket”, noun), from consoler (“to console, to comfort”, verb).
Sense of “bracket” either due to a bracket alleviating the load, or due to brackets being decorated with the Christian figure of a consolateur (“consoler”), itself perhaps a pun on the first sense (alleviating load).
Originally used for the bracket itself, then for wall-mounted tables (mounted with a bracket), then for free-standing tables placed against a wall. Use for control system dates at least to 1880s for an “organ console”; use for electrical or electronic control systems dates at least to 1

ex.en: With this his spirit will be consoled.
ex.ja: これで彼の霊も浮かばれるだろう。

ex.en: I consoled him with his favorite food.
ex.ja: 私は彼の好きな食べ物で彼を元気付けた。

ex.en: The grieving woman was consoled by her friends.
ex.ja: 悲しみに暮れるその女性は友人たちに慰められた。

note.ja: 「慰める」はラテン語 consolari ＝ con + solari（慰める）。「操作盤」はフランス語 console（壁から出た支え）からで別語。

en: A person or company that builds or improves buildings or structures.
A person or company that performs specific tasks like electrical or plumbing work in construction projects.

contractor.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin contractor, from Latin contract-, stem of contractus + -tor. First attested in the 16th century.

ex.en: I cannot calculate the final cost until I talk with our contractors.
ex.ja: 契約者と話すまでは最終的な予算を計算することはできません。

ex.en: Right on schedule, that contractor came around today, begging for more time.
ex.ja: 予定通りに、その業者は、時間がもう少し欲しい、と言ってきた。

ex.en: Just like I thought, the contractor came back today, begging for more time.
ex.ja: 案の定、あの業者今日になって泣きついてきたよ。

note.ja: con（共に）+ tract（引く）+ or。契約（contract）を結ぶ人 →「請負業者」。

The length of such a line.

ex.en: The diameter of the hole was slightly larger.
ex.ja: その穴の直径のほうがわずかに大きかった。

ex.en: Is it possible to determine the diameter from the circumference?
ex.ja: 円周から直径を求めることは可能ですか？

ex.en: Earth has a diameter of 12,742 kilometers.
ex.ja: 地球の直径は、12,742キロです。

note.ja: dia（横切って）+ meter（測る）。円を横切って測った長さ →「直径」。

en: A place where waste or garbage is left; a ground or place for dumping ashes, refuse, etc.; a disposal site.
A car or boat for dumping refuse, etc.
To release, especially in large quantities and chaotic manner.
To discard; to get rid of something one no longer wants.

dump.ety: From Middle English dumpen, dompen, probably from Old Norse dumpa (“to thump”) (whence Danish dumpe (“to fall suddenly”)), of uncertain origin, possibly imitative of falling, similar to thump.

ex.en: The truck dumped the sand on the ground.
ex.ja: トラックは砂を地面にどさっと落した。

ex.en: After Tom dumped Mary, she started seeing John.
ex.ja: メアリーはトムにフラれてからジョンと付き合い始めた。

ex.en: I got dumped by my girlfriend last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜、彼女に振られた。

note.ja: 北欧語 dumpa（どさっと落ちる）から。擬音的な語。「捨てる」→「ごみ捨て場」→（口語）恋人を「振る」。

en: Two people who work or collaborate together as partners; especially
Two musicians who perform music together.

ex.en: Duo, the owl, teaches many languages.
ex.ja: ふくろうのDuoは、たくさんの言語を教えてます。

note.ja: イタリア語 duo（2）から。→「二人組・二重奏」。dual、double と同じ duo。

ex.ja: ボストンダイナミクスは走ることさえ出来るロボットを造りましたよ。

en: A large mammal of the family Elephantidae in the order Proboscidea, having a trunk, and native to Africa and Asia.
Anything huge and ponderous.

elephant.ety: From Middle English elefant, elefaunt, from Old French elefant, elefan, olifant, re-latinized in Middle French as elephant, from Latin elephantus, from Ancient Greek ἐλέφᾱς (eléphās) (gen. ἐλέφαντος (eléphantos)). Believed to be derived from an Afroasiatic form such as Proto-Berber *eḷu (“elephant”) (compare Tamahaq êlu, Tamasheq alu) or Egyptian ꜣbw (“elephant; ivory”). More at ivory. Replaced Middle English olifant (from the aforementioned Old French form, from Vulgar Latin *olifantus), which replaced Old English elpend (“elephant”).

ex.en: Elephants are the largest land animals alive today.
ex.ja: 今日、象は現存する最も大きい陸生動物である。

ex.en: This is how they catch an elephant alive.
ex.ja: こんなふうにして彼らは象を生け捕りにする。

ex.en: This is the way they capture elephants alive.
ex.ja: こんなふうにして彼らは象を生け捕りにする。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 elephas（象・象牙）から。→「象」。

en: To augment or make something greater.
To improve something by adding features.

enhance.ety: From Middle English enhauncen, anhaunsen, from Anglo-Norman anhauncer (“enhance, raise”), from Vulgar Latin *inaltiāre (“raise”), derived from Latin in + altus (“high”). The /h/ in Old French was taken from haut (“high”), where it resulted from Frankish influence.

ex.en: So-called "winter time" is expected to enhance the college reform.
ex.ja: 「冬の時代」が大学改革の起爆剤となってくれればと思う。

ex.en: If you have a good garden, it will enhance the value of your house.
ex.ja: よい庭がついていれば家の価値を高めるでしょう。

ex.en: Garlic enhances the flavor of meals.
ex.ja: にんにくは食事の風味を増す。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ hance（高い）。ラテン語 altus（高い）から。高める →「高める・向上させる」。

en: To draw or let out wholly; to drain completely.
To empty by drawing or letting out the contents.
A system consisting of the parts of an engine through which burned gases or steam are discharged; see also exhaust system.
The steam let out of a cylinder after it has done its work there.

From Latin exhaustus, past participle of exhaurīre (“to draw out, drink up, empty, exhaust”), from ex (“out”) + haurīre (“to draw (especially water), drain”).

ex.en: I felt exhausted when the game was over.
ex.ja: ゲームが終わったときには私は疲れ切っていた。

ex.en: I exhausted myself by walking a long distance.
ex.ja: 長い距離を歩いて疲れ果てた。

ex.en: I can't do it. I'm just so exhausted.
ex.ja: もうダメだ、もうくたくた、疲れた。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ haust（くみ出す）。くみ尽くす →「使い果たす・疲れ果てさせる・排気ガス」。

en: The physical material of a building.
The framework underlying a structure.
To cover with fabric.

fabric.ety: Borrowed from French fabrique, from Latin fabrica (“a workshop, art, trade, product of art, structure, fabric”), from faber (“artisan, workman”). Doublet of fabrica, borrowed from Latin, and forge, borrowed from Old French.

ex.en: Thank you for your letter of July 25 and the fabric sample.
ex.ja: ７月２５日付の御手紙と布地のサンプルありがとうございました。

ex.en: I'd like to have this fabric dyed.
ex.ja: この織物を染めて欲しいのです。

ex.en: I reached into the pile and felt soft fabric.
ex.ja: 私はその山に手を入れて柔らかい織物に触れた。

note.ja: ラテン語 fabrica（工房・作られたもの）から。faber（職人）。→「布地・構造」。fabricate（作り上げる・でっち上げる）。

Characteristic of fables; marvelous, extraordinary, incredible.

ex.en: I can't imagine anything more fabulous.
ex.ja: これ以上素晴らしいものは想像もつかないわ。

ex.en: He has a fabulous reputation for his high integrity.
ex.ja: 彼は高潔なことで非常に評判が高い。

ex.en: The laboratory acquired a fabulous reputation for its historic discovery.
ex.ja: その研究所はその歴史的な発見によってすばらしい評判を得た。

note.ja: ラテン語 fabulosus（伝説的な）から。fabula（物語）。「物語に出てくるような」→「すばらしい」。fable と同じ。

en: A mythical being of human form with magical powers, known in many sizes and descriptions, although typically depicted as a small sprite w…
An attractive young woman; a small, graceful woman.
Like a fairy; fanciful, whimsical, delicate.

fairy.ety: From Middle English faierie, fairie, from Old French faerie, from fae (from Latin fāta (“goddess of fate”)) + -erie. Equivalent to fay + -ry. Attested in English from about 1330, in King Alisaunder, first in the sense of "enchantment, illusion, dream" ("that thou herdest is fairye") and shortly thereafter "realm of the fays, fairy-land" and "the inhabitants of fairyland, collectively". The re-interpretation of the term as a countable noun denoting individual inhabitants of fairy-land can be traced to the 1390s, but became common only in the 16th century, perhaps due to reinterpreting phrases l

ex.en: The fairy changed the prince into a cat.
ex.ja: 妖精は王子を猫に変えた。

ex.en: Did you write this fairy tale by yourself?
ex.ja: あなたはこの童話を一人で書いたのですか。

ex.en: I had fairy tales read by my mother.
ex.ja: 私はお母さんにおとぎ話を読んでもらった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 faerie（妖精の国）から。ラテン語 fata（運命の女神）にさかのぼる。fate と同じ祖先。

en: To bend (any thin material, such as paper) over so that it comes in contact with itself.
To make the proper arrangement (in a thin material) by bending.
An act of folding.
Any correct move in origami.

fold.ety:
The verb is from Middle English folden, from Old English fealdan, from Proto-West Germanic *falþan, from Proto-Germanic *falþaną (“to fold”), from Proto-Indo-European *pel- (“to fold”).
Cognate with Dutch vouwen, German falten.
The noun is from Middle English folde, falde, itself derived from the verb.

ex.en: John was standing alone with his arms folded.
ex.ja: ジョンは腕を組んだまま一人で立っていた。

ex.en: Her fingers were too weak to fold it.
ex.ja: 折ろうとしても指が弱くなりすぎていた。

ex.en: He just looked on with his arms folded.
ex.ja: 彼はただ手をこまねいて見ているだけだった。

note.ja: 古英語 fealdan から。「折りたたむ」。-fold（〜倍）も同じ語。羊の「囲い」は別語。

en: Foiled, stopped, disappointed.
Suffering from frustration; dissatisfied, agitated, discontent and/or slightly angry because one is unable to perform an action or fulfil…

ex.en: Illness frustrated his plans for the trip.
ex.ja: 病気で彼の旅行の計画は挫折した。

ex.en: You are frustrated with your work.
ex.ja: 君は仕事に欲求不満を感じている。

ex.en: The bad weather frustrated our plans.
ex.ja: 悪天候のために私たちの計画はだめになった。

note.ja: frustrate（挫折させる）+ -ed。ラテン語 frustra（無駄に）。「無駄にされた」→「不満な」。

en: An activity characterized by a balance between winning and losing that is governed by skill or chance, usually with money wagered on the …

ex.en: Both my father and my brother like gambling.
ex.ja: 私の父も兄もどちらも賭事が好きです。

ex.en: You've got to give up gambling once and for all.
ex.ja: ギャンブルはきっぱりと止めなさい。

ex.en: Gambling was by no means his only source of income.
ex.ja: ギャンブルが彼の唯一の収入源というわけでは決してなかった。

note.ja: game（遊び）から作られた gamble（賭ける）+ ing。→「賭博・ギャンブル」。

en: Without strong force or quickness: softly, lightly.
In a gentle manner; to a gentle degree.

gently.ety: From Middle English gentilly, gentlych, gentilliche, equivalent to gentle + -ly, with *-lely simplified to -ly by haplology.

ex.ja: 彼は彼女の肩にそっと手を置いた。

ex.en: Mary gently placed her hand on his shoulder.
ex.ja: メアリーは彼の肩にそっと手を置いた。

ex.en: She laid the child down gently.
ex.ja: 彼女は子供をそっと寝かせた。

note.ja: gentle（優しい）+ -ly。「優しく」。gentle はラテン語 gentilis（同じ一族の・家柄のよい）。

en: Exhibiting attributes, qualities, or acts that are worthy of or receive glory.
Excellent, wonderful; delightful.

glorious.ety: From Middle English glorious, from Anglo-Norman glorius and Old French glorïos, from Latin glōriōsus. Displaced native Middle English wulderful, from Old English wuldorfull (“glorious”), among other terms. Equivalent to glory + -ous.

ex.en: We had a glorious time at the seaside.
ex.ja: 私達は海岸ですばらしいひとときを過ごした。

ex.en: We had a glorious time.
ex.ja: 素敵な楽しいひと時でした。

ex.en: A glorious sight burst on our view.
ex.ja: すばらしい景色がさっと目の前に現れた。

note.ja: ラテン語 gloria（栄光）から。→「栄光ある・輝かしい・素晴らしい」。

en: Suffering, hardship.
Emotional pain, generally arising from misfortune, significant personal loss, bereavement, misconduct of oneself or others, etc.; sorrow;…

grief.ety: From Middle English greef, gref, from Old French grief (“grave, heavy, grievous, sad”), from Latin gravis (“heavy, grievous, sad”). Doublet of grave.

ex.en: He was the agent of her grief.
ex.ja: 彼女の悲しみの原因は彼だった。

ex.en: Crying is an expression of grief.
ex.ja: 泣く事は悲しみの表現だ。

ex.en: This will bring you to grief.
ex.ja: 後で憂き目をみる。

note.ja: ラテン語 gravis（重い）から。心が重いこと →「深い悲しみ」。grieve（深く悲しむ）。

en: In a historic manner; with reference to history or the historical record.
According to history: formerly, in the past, traditionally.

ex.ja: フォークを使う人々は、歴史的にみて、ずっと少数派であった。

note.ja: historical + -ly。「歴史的に」。

en: The central part, usually cylindrical, of a wheel; the nave.
A point where many routes meet and traffic is distributed, dispensed, or diverted.

hub.ety: From earlier hubbe, which has the same immediate origin as hob. Hub was originally a dialectal word; its ultimate origin is unknown. Compare German Hubbel (“bump on a surface”), from Proto-West Germanic *hubil (“bump, hill”) (which contains a diminutive suffix *-il); compare English hive, or perhaps ultimately from the same root as hip or hop.

ex.en: If you combine them in this way, you get a 14 port USB hub.
ex.ja: こういう風に合体すれば、１４ポートのＵＳＢハブになります。

note.ja: 車輪の「こしき（中心部）」から。語源ははっきりしない。「中心・拠点」。

en: Impossible to avoid or prevent.
Predictable or always happening.
Something that is predictable, necessary, or cannot be avoided.

inevitable.ety: From Middle French inevitable, from Latin inēvītābilis (“unavoidable”), from in- + ēvītābilis (“avoidable”), from ēvītāre (“to avoid”), from ē- (“out”) + vītāre (“to shun”).

ex.en: The Foreign Minister said that war was inevitable.
ex.ja: 外相は、戦争は避けられないと言った。

ex.en: It was inevitable that they would meet.
ex.ja: 彼らが会うことは避けられなかった。

ex.en: It is inevitable that some changes will take place.
ex.ja: 必ず変化が起こるだろう。

note.ja: in（否定）+ e（外へ）+ vit（避ける）+ able。ラテン語 evitare（避ける）から。避けられない →「必然の・避けられない」。

ex.ja: 彼の良さは外見では分からない。

Such stories as a genre.

ex.ja: その山は神話や伝説でよく知られている。

ex.ja: 彼は古代神話に基づく小説を書いた。

ex.en: What he had said proved to be a myth.
ex.ja: 彼の話は作りごとだったとわかった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mythos（言葉・物語）から。→「神話・作り話・根拠のない通説」。

ex.ja: どうしてそんなに彼女にこだわるの？

ex.ja: なんでそんなに彼に夢中なの？

ex.ja: 細かなほこりが空中に浮いている。

en: A minister or priest in a church.
The main priest serving a parish.
To serve a congregation as pastor.

ex.ja: その少女は、目を閉じて牧師の話を聞いた。

ex.en: Bob became a pastor.
ex.ja: ボブは牧師になりました。

ex.ja: ４０代になるまでは牧師になるべきではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 pastor（羊飼い）から。信者という羊を導く人 →「牧師」。pasture（牧草地）。

en: In a permanent manner; lastingly.
Forever.

permanently.ety: From Middle English permanently; equivalent to permanent + -ly.

ex.en: I've had my hair removed permanently, so my skin is smooth.
ex.ja: 私は今は永久脱毛で肌がツルツルです。

note.ja: permanent（永続的な）+ -ly。per（通して）+ manere（とどまる）。「ずっととどまる」→「永久に」。remain と同じ man。

Anything harmful to a person or thing.
To use poison to kill or paralyse (somebody).
To pollute; to cause to become poisonous.

ex.ja: 彼は妻を毒殺したと言われている。

ex.en: Eating raw chicken can give you food poisoning.
ex.ja: 生の鶏肉を食べると食中毒を起こすことがあります。

A person belonging to a province; one who is provincial.
A monastic superior, who, under the general of his order, has the direction of all the religious houses of the same fraternity in a given…

ex.ja: 彼の態度から彼が地方出身なことは明らかだ。

To forcefully subvert the law of the land in an attempt to replace it with another form of government.

ex.ja: 彼はそこで反徒の襲撃を受けた。

ex.ja: その学生達は政府に対して反抗した。

note.ja: re（再び）+ bel（戦う）。ラテン語 bellum（戦争）から。再び戦いを起こす →「反逆者・反抗する」。

Relating to tragedy in a literary work.
