To lose liquid.
To flow gradually.

drain.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *dʰer-der.
Proto-Indo-European *dʰrewgʰ-der.
Proto-Germanic *draugiz
Proto-Germanic *drauhnōną
Proto-West Germanic *drauhnōn
Old English drēahnian
Middle English *dreinen
English drain
Inherited from Middle English *dreinen, from Old English drēahnian, from Proto-West Germanic *drauhnōn, from Proto-Germanic *drauhnōną, from *draugiz, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrewgʰ-, from *dʰer-. Akin to Old English drūgian (“to dry up”), Old English drūgaþ (“dryness, drought”), Old English drȳġe (“dry”). More at dry.

ex.en: The school drains the pool once a month.
ex.ja: 学校はプールの水を月一回排水する。

ex.en: All the color drained away from his face.
ex.ja: 彼の顔からすっかり血の気が引いていった。

ex.en: The water will soon drain away.
ex.ja: 水はすぐにはけるだろう。

note.ja: 古英語 drēahnian（水気を切る）から。dry と同系。「排水する」→「消耗させる」。

en: Something which is emitted or sent out; issue.
The act of emitting; the act of sending forth or putting into circulation.

emission.ety: First attested in 1607. From Middle French émission, from Latin ēmissiō (“sending forth”), from ēmittō (“send out”), from ex (“from, out of”) + mittō (“send”).

ex.en: His mobile phone produced radio emissions that interfered with other phones.
ex.ja: 彼の携帯電話は他の電話を妨害する電波を出した。

ex.en: Industrial emissions cause air pollution.
ex.ja: 工場の排気ガスが大気を汚染している。

ex.en: It is said that global warming is directly related to carbon dioxide emissions.
ex.ja: 地球温暖化は二酸化炭素の排出と直接関係があると言われている。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ miss（送る）+ ion。外へ送り出すこと →「排出・放射」。

en: Of or relating to the study of ethics.
Of or relating to the accepted principles of right and wrong, especially those of some organization or profession.
An ethical drug, one only dispensed on the prescription of a physician.

ethical.ety: From ethic + -al, from Late Latin ethicus (“moral, ethical”), from Ancient Greek ἠθικός (ēthikós, “of or for morals, moral, expressing character”), from ἦθος (êthos, “character, moral nature”).

ex.en: In ethical terms, a great many people are opposed to gene therapy.
ex.ja: 倫理の面で、たくさんの人々が遺伝子治療に反対している。

ex.en: It is not ethical for a doctor to reveal confidences.
ex.ja: 医師が患者の秘密を漏らすのは道義にもとる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ēthos（習慣・人柄）から。→「倫理的な・道徳上の」。ethics（倫理学）。

en: The quality of being excellent; brilliance
Something in which one excels.

excellence.ety: From Middle English excellence, from Old French excellence, from Latin excellentia.

ex.en: He won the prize for excellence in all subjects.
ex.ja: 彼は全科目優等で賞を得た。

ex.en: We fully appreciate his excellence as a skier.
ex.ja: 彼のスキーヤーとしての優秀性は十分に買っています。

ex.en: We were amazed at the excellence of the boy's drawings.
ex.ja: 私たちはその少年のデッサンのすばらしさに驚嘆した。

note.ja: ラテン語 excellere（抜きん出る）から。ex（外へ）+ cellere（そびえる）。→「優秀さ・卓越」。excellent（優れた）。

en: The visible part of fire; a stream of burning vapour or gas, emitting light and heat.
A romantic partner or lover in a usually short-lived but passionate affair.
Of a brilliant reddish orange-gold colour, like that of a flame.
To produce flames; to burn with a flame or blaze.
To burst forth like flame; to break out in violence of passion; to be kindled with zeal or ardour.

flame.ety: From Middle English flawme, blend of Old French flame and flambe, flamble, the first from Latin flamma, the second from Latin flammula, diminutive of flamma, both from pre-Latin *fladma; Proto-Italic *flagmā, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to shimmer, gleam, shine”). Displaced native Old English līeġ.

ex.en: The forest was in flames for three days.
ex.ja: 森は３日間炎を出して燃えていた。

ex.en: I would love to see my old flame again.
ex.ja: 昔の恋人に再会してみたい。

ex.en: She gave herself to flames of love.
ex.ja: 彼女は恋の炎に身を焼いた。

note.ja: ラテン語 flamma（炎）から古フランス語を経た語。flamingo（炎の色の鳥）と同じ。

en: Free; frank.
Generous; noble; excellent; beautiful; lovely.
In a free manner.
Without interference or restriction.

freely.ety: From Middle English frely, freelich, from Old English frēolīc (“free, freeborn, glorious, stately, magnificent, noble, beautiful, charming”), equivalent to free + -ly. Compare Middle Low German vrilik, vrigelik (“free”), Middle High German vrīlich (“free”).

ex.en: The second language may be freely chosen.
ex.ja: 第二外国語は自由に選択できることになっている。

ex.en: Now that Father is gone, we can talk freely.
ex.ja: 父が行ってしまったから、我々は自由に話が出来る。

ex.en: You can enter the library freely.
ex.ja: 皆さんは自由に図書館に入れる。

note.ja: free（自由な）+ -ly。「自由に・気前よく」。

en: The action or process of graduating and receiving a diploma for completing a course of study (such as from an educational institution).
A commencement ceremony.

ex.en: The student council discussed plans for the graduation.
ex.ja: 生徒会は卒業式の計画について話し合った。

ex.en: After graduation he will engage himself in study.
ex.ja: 彼は卒業後、研究に従事するだろう。

ex.en: What do you plan to do after graduation?
ex.ja: 卒業したらどうするつもりですか。

note.ja: graduate（卒業する）+ -ion。ラテン語 gradus（段）。「学位の段階を上がること」→「卒業」、「目盛り」。grade、gradually と同じ。

en: A clue.
An implicit suggestion that avoids a direct statement.
To imply without a direct statement; to provide a clue.
To bring to mind by a slight mention or remote allusion; to suggest in an indirect manner.
Signifies that something previously said should be taken as a hint or heeded closely.

hint.ety: From Middle English hinten, hynten, variant of henten (“to lay hold of, catch”), from Old English hentan (“to seize, grasp”), from Proto-West Germanic *hantijan, from Proto-Germanic *hantijaną. Doublet of hent. Related also to hunt.

ex.en: They didn't so much as hint at it.
ex.ja: 彼らはその事をほのめかしさえしなかった。

ex.en: The speaker hinted at corruption in the political world.
ex.ja: 講演者は政界の腐敗をほのめかした。

ex.en: There was a hint of fall in the air.
ex.ja: 秋の気配が感じられた。

note.ja: 中英語 hent（つかむこと）から。「つかみどころ」→「ヒント・ほのめかし」。

en: The visible horizontal line (in all directions) where the sky appears to meet the earth in the distance.
The range or limit of one's knowledge, experience or interest; a boundary or threshold.

horizon.ety: Inherited from Middle English orisonte, orisoun, from Middle French horizon, horizonte, from Old French orisonte, orison, via Latin horizōn, from Ancient Greek ὁρίζων (horízōn), from ὅρος (hóros, “boundary”).

ex.en: We saw the sun rise above the horizon.
ex.ja: 私たちは太陽が地平線に昇るのを見た。

ex.en: Do you see a ship on the horizon?
ex.ja: 水平線に船が見えますか。

ex.en: By and by the moon appeared on the horizon.
ex.ja: やがて月が地平線上に現れた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 horizōn（境界を定める円）から。→「地平線・水平線・視野」。horizontal（水平な）。

en: Not friendly; appropriate to an enemy; showing the disposition of an enemy; showing ill will and malevolence or a desire to thwart and in…
Aggressive; antagonistic.
An enemy.

hostile.ety: Borrowed from Middle French hostile, from Latin hostīlis, from hostis (“enemy”). Displaced Old English fēondlīċ.

ex.en: I see that I'm surrounded by hostile faces.
ex.ja: これじゃあまるで四面楚歌だ。

ex.en: The Soviet Union took a hostile attitude toward us.
ex.ja: ソ連はわが国に対して強い態度をとった。

ex.en: I see that I am surrounded by hostile faces.
ex.ja: これじゃあまるで四面楚歌だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 hostis（敵・よそ者）から。host（主人）、hospital（病院）と遠い親戚。→「敵意のある・敵の」。

en: Someone or thing who lives in a place.
A possible value for a type.
resident

inhabitant.ety: From Middle English inhabitantes (n. plural) and inhabitaunt (adj.), from Old French inhabitant, from Latin inhabitāns, present participle of inhabitō (“to inhabit”), from in- (“in”) + habitō (“to dwell”) (frequentative of habeō (“to hold”), from Proto-Indo-European *ghabh- (“to seize, take, hold, have”). By surface analysis, inhabit + -ant.

ex.en: The plan met with opposition from the inhabitants.
ex.ja: その計画は住民の反対にあった。

ex.en: The inhabitants are proud of their urban culture.
ex.ja: 住民達は彼らの都会的な文化に誇りを持っている。

ex.en: The inhabitants of the island are friendly.
ex.ja: その島の住民は友好的だ。

note.ja: in（中に）+ hab（持つ・住む）+ it + ant（人）。中に住んでいる人 →「住民」。

en: A pigment (or dye)-based fluid used for writing, printing etc.
A particular type, color or container of this fluid.
To apply ink to; to cover or smear with ink.
To sign (a contract or similar document).

ink.ety:
From Middle English ynke, from Old French enque, from Latin encaustum (“purple ink used by Roman emperors to sign documents”), from Ancient Greek ἔγκαυστον (énkauston, “burned-in”), from ἐν (en, “in”) + καίω (kaíō, “burn”). In this sense, displaced native Old English blæc (“ink”, literally “black”).
Sense four refers to the ink used in newspapers.

ex.en: I always write letters with pen and ink.
ex.ja: 私はいつもペンで手紙を書いています。

ex.en: Sir, do we have to write in ink?
ex.ja: 先生、ペン書きにするのでしょうか。

ex.en: The sale prices are written in red ink.
ex.ja: 特価品の値段は、赤インクで書かれている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 enkauston（焼きつけた紫のインク）から古フランス語を経た語。encaustic（焼き付け画法）と同じ。

en: Any establishment where travellers can procure lodging, food, and drink.
A tavern.

inn.ety: From Middle English in, inn, from Old English inn (“a dwelling, house, chamber, lodging”); akin to Icelandic inni (“a dwelling place, home, abode”), Faroese inni (“home”).

ex.en: He proposed that they stay at that inn.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らにその旅館に泊まるように言った。

ex.en: He proposed that they put up at that inn.
ex.ja: 彼はその部屋に泊まろうと提案した。

ex.en: I spent 2 nights at a mountain Inn.
ex.ja: 山間の旅館で２泊しました。

note.ja: 古英語 inn（家・宿）から。in（中に）と同じ語。「中に入る所」→「宿屋」。

en: The cavity or mold in which anything is formed.
The metaphorical place where something is made, formed, or given birth.

matrix.ety:
From Middle English matris, matrice, matrix, from Old French matrice (“pregnant animal”), or from Latin mātrīx (“dam, womb”), both ultimately from māter (“mother”). Doublet of mother from Indo-European ancestor.
Slang usage coined with the 1999 sci-fi action film The Matrix.

note.ja: ラテン語 mater（母）から。母胎 →（ものを生み出す）「基盤・母体・行列」。

en: In a state of misery: very sad, ill, or poor.
Very bad (at something); unskilled, incompetent; hopeless.
A miserable person; a wretch.
A state of misery or melancholy.

miserable.ety: Borrowed from Middle French miserable, from Old French, from Latin miserabilis, equivalent to miser + -able.

ex.en: The sight was too miserable to look at.
ex.ja: その光景は目も当てられなかった。

ex.en: Because of her, he lived a miserable life.
ex.ja: 彼女のおかげで彼はみじめな暮らしをした。

ex.en: The experiment resulted in a miserable failure.
ex.ja: その実験は惨めな失敗に終わった。

note.ja: ラテン語 miserabilis（哀れな）から。miser（哀れな）。「惨めな」。misery、miserably と同じ。

en: Of a body in motion: the tendency of a body to maintain its inertial motion; the product of its mass and velocity, or the vector sum of t…
Strength or force gained by motion or movement.

momentum.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-yeti

Latin mōmentumbor.
English momentum
Borrowed from Latin mōmentum. Doublet of moment and movement.

ex.en: As the days passed, our campaign grew in momentum.
ex.ja: 日がたつにつれて我々の運動ははずみがついた。

note.ja: ラテン語 momentum（動き）から。movere（動かす）。→「勢い・運動量」。moment（瞬間）と同語源。

en: A member of the clade Simiiformes other than those in the clade Hominoidea containing apes, generally (but not universally) distinguished…
Any simian, including humans.
To meddle; to mess (with).
To mimic; to ape.

monkey.ety:
Uncertain:
* May be derived from monk + -ey (diminutive suffix),
* or borrowed from Middle Low German Moneke, the name of the son of Martin the Ape in Reynard the Fox (which may represent an unattested colloquial Middle Low German *moneke, *moneken), itself of uncertain origin:
** Possibly derived from a Romance term represented by Late Middle French monne (whence Modern French mone (“monkey”)) or earlier Old French monnekin (“monkey”), originally Monnekin, the name of a monkey in Li Dis d'Entendement. Compare also Old French and Middle French monin (“monkey”).
*** The French terms may have be

ex.en: She was fat, and holding a monkey.
ex.ja: デブっている彼女は、猿を抱きかかえていた。

ex.en: Not a few monkeys were found in the mountain.
ex.ja: その山で少なからぬ猿が発見された。

ex.en: There are many monkeys on the mountain.
ex.ja: その山にはたくさんサルがいる。

note.ja: 語源は未確定。低地ドイツ語の物語『ライネケ狐』に登場するサルの子 Moneke に由来する説や、ロマンス諸語の monna（猿）、monk + 指小辞とする説などがある。

en: An open-seated motor vehicle with handlebars instead of a steering wheel, and having two (or sometimes three) wheels.
To ride a motorcycle.

motorcycle.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *m(y)ewh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *-yeti
Proto-Indo-European *-éyeti
Proto-Indo-European *m(y)owh₁éyeti
Proto-Italic *moweō
Latin moveō
Proto-Indo-European *-tōr

Latin -tor
Latin mōtorder.
Middle English motour
English motor

Proto-Indo-European *-os
Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos
Proto-Hellenic *kʷókʷlos
Proto-Hellenic *kúklos
Ancient Greek κύκλος (kúklos)der.
Late Latin cyclusbor.
Middle English cicle
English cycle
English motorcycle
From motor + cycle, from the Motorcyclette produced in 1897 by the French We

ex.en: I don't know how much this motorcycle is.
ex.ja: このオートバイがいくらか、私は知りません。

ex.en: Why don't you have your motorcycle fixed up?
ex.ja: オートバイを修理してもらいなさいよ。

ex.en: You can have a ride on my motorcycle.
ex.ja: 私のバイクに乗ってもいいですよ。

note.ja: motor（モーター）+ cycle（車輪）。「オートバイ」。bicycle と同じ cycle。

en: Extending throughout an entire nation.
Throughout a nation.

nationwide.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *ǵénh₁tisder.
Proto-Italic *gnātiō
Latin nātiōlbor.
Old French nacionbor.
Middle English nacioun
English nation
Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁
Proto-Indo-European *dwi-
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *h₁weydʰh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *-ós
Proto-Indo-European *h₁weydʰh₁ós
Proto-Germanic *wīdaz
Old English wīd
English wide
English -wide
English nationwide
From nation + -wide.

ex.en: The police have started a nationwide hunt for the criminal.
ex.ja: 警察は犯人の全国的な捜索を開始した。

ex.en: They have formed their own nationwide association, the American Association of Retired Persons.
ex.ja: 彼らは、アメリカ退職者協会という独自の全国組織を結成している。

ex.en: He had got nationwide fame.
ex.ja: 彼は全国的名声があった。

note.ja: nation（国）+ wide（全体に広がった）。「全国的な」。worldwide と同じ作り。

en: A structure built by a bird as a place to incubate eggs and rear young.
A structure built, or site modified, to incubate eggs, rear young, or shelter a colony.
To build or settle into a nest.
To settle into a home.

nest.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁en-?
Proto-Indo-European *ní
Proto-Indo-European *sed-
Proto-Indo-European *-ós
Proto-Indo-European *nisdós
Proto-Germanic *nestą
Proto-West Germanic *nest
Old English nest
Middle English nest
English nest
From Middle English nest, nist, nyst, from Old English nest, from Proto-West Germanic *nest, from Proto-Germanic *nestą, from Proto-Indo-European *nisdós (“nest”), literally "where [the bird] sits down", a compound of *ni (“down”) (whence also English nether) + the zero-grade of the root *sed- (“to sit”) (whence also English sit).

ex.en: We may be able to see birds' nests.
ex.ja: 鳥の巣が見られるかもしれない。

ex.en: She carefully watched the bird in the nest.
ex.ja: 彼女は巣の中の鳥を注意して見つめた。

ex.en: Can you see the nest in the tree?
ex.ja: 木の上に巣があるのが見える？

note.ja: 核のイメージは「巣」。ラテン語 nidus と同じ祖先 ＝ ni（下に）+ sed（座る）。鳥が座り込む場所。

en: Precisely; with fine discernment or judgement.
Pleasantly; satisfactorily.

nicely.ety: From Middle English nycely; equivalent to nice + -ly.

ex.en: The translation was nicely true to the original.
ex.ja: その翻訳は原作に見事に忠実であった。

ex.en: He's coming along nicely with his studies.
ex.ja: 彼は勉強がうまく進んでいる。

ex.en: This page is not nicely printed so print it again.
ex.ja: このページ、きれいに印刷できてないから、もう一度やり直して。

note.ja: nice + -ly。「うまく・すてきに」。nice はラテン語 nescius（無知な）から「愚かな」→「細かい」→「よい」と意味が大きく変わった。

en: The ordinal form of the number nine.
The person or thing in the ninth position.
One of nine equal parts of a whole.
To lose a ninth.
To divide by nine.

ninth.ety: From Middle English nynthe, nynte, from Old English niġoþa, from Proto-Germanic *newundô; the -n- was reinserted by analogy with nine. Equivalent to nine + -th (ordinal suffix).

ex.en: Tell me the name of the ninth month.
ex.ja: 第９番目の月の名を言ってごらん。

ex.en: I was in the ninth grade last year.
ex.ja: 私は去年中学３年生だった。

ex.en: September is the ninth month of the year.
ex.ja: 「９月」は１年の中で９回目の月にあたります。

note.ja: nine の序数。e を落として ninth とつづる。

en: An act or instance of nominating.
The result of such a nomination act.

nomination.ety: From Middle English nominacion, nomination, from Middle French nominacion and its etymon Latin nōminātiō, from the verb nōminō (“to name; to nominate”). By surface analysis, nominate + -ion.

ex.en: I second his nomination.
ex.ja: 私は彼を指名するのを支持します。

ex.en: She won an Oscar nomination for best supporting actress.
ex.ja: 彼女はアカデミー賞の最優秀助演女優にノミネートされた。

ex.en: Forty-seven men wanted the nomination.
ex.ja: 四十七人が指名を望んでいた。

note.ja: nom（名前）+ ination。名前を挙げること →「指名・ノミネート」。

en: Worthy of note; remarkable; memorable; noted or distinguished.
Easily noted (without connotations of value); clearly noticeable, conspicuous.
A person or thing of distinction.

notable.ety: Inherited from Middle English notable (“worthy of note, profitable, useful”), in some senses from Anglo-Norman notable (“noteworthy”), from Latin notābilis (“noteworthy, extraordinary”), from notō (“to note, mark”); in some senses from Middle English note (“benefit, profit, use, advantage”), from Old English notu (“t-use, profit, advantage, employment”) + -able; equivalent to note + -able. Compare English noteful (“useful”).

ex.en: Chemistry has made notable progress in recent years.
ex.ja: 近年、化学は驚くべき進歩を遂げてきた。

ex.en: Our century has seen a notable increase of knowledge.
ex.ja: 今世紀には注目すべき知識の増加があった。

ex.en: The area is notable for its scenery and wildlife.
ex.ja: その地域は風景と野生動物で注目に値する。

note.ja: note（注目する）+ able。注目に値する →「注目すべき・著名な」。

en: The act of binding oneself by a social, legal, or moral tie to someone.
A social, legal, or moral requirement, duty, contract, or promise that compels someone to follow or avoid a particular course of action.

obligation.ety: From Middle English obligacioun, from Old French obligacion, from Latin obligatio, obligationem, from obligatum (past participle of obligare), from ob- (“to”) + ligare (“to bind”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyǵ- (“to bind”).

ex.en: You have no obligation to help us.
ex.ja: あなたは我々を援助する必要はない。

ex.en: We have a legal obligation to pay our taxes.
ex.ja: 私達は税金を払う義務がある。

ex.en: Every player is under obligation to keep the rules.
ex.ja: 選手はすべてルールを守る義務がある。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ lig（縛る）+ ation。縛りつけるもの →「義務」。oblige（義務を負わせる）、religion も同じ lig とされる。

en: Of or relating to sight; visual.
Designed to assist or enhance sight
Any special effect requiring laboratory work on the film.

From optic + -al.

ex.en: This looks longer than that, but it is an optical illusion.
ex.ja: これはあれよりも長いように見えるが、錯覚だ。

ex.en: Lenses with two distinct optical powers are also called "bifocals".
ex.ja: 二重焦点レンズは「バイフォーカル」とも呼ばれる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 optikos（視覚の）から。「光学の・視覚の」。optician（眼鏡屋）と同じ。

The view from such a place.

reed.ety:
From Middle English red, from Old English hrēod, from Proto-West Germanic *hreud (“reed”), of uncertain origin.
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian raid (“reed”), Saterland Frisian Räit (“reed”), West Frisian reid (“reed”), Dutch riet (“reed”), German Reet, Ried (“reed”). No cognates in North Germanic languages, but the existence of an otherwise unattested Gothic *𐌷𐍂𐌹𐌿𐌳 (*hriud) was supposed by the brothers Grimm. They also theorised that the word may have a relation to the retas mentioned in Noctes Atticae (Aulus Gellius). The measuring reed sense is the translation of Akkadian qanûm ("cane")
